You could not be more wrong.  You are not allowed to bomb civilian objects. Attacks may be directed only at military objectives.

The starting rule is the opposite of what you wrote. Houses, apartments, schools, mosques, churches, hospitals, and shops are civilian objects. If an object is normally used for civilian purposes, it is presumed civilian. You do not get to treat it as a military target unless you can show that that specific object, at the time of the attack:

is making an effective contribution to military action by its nature, location, purpose, or use, and
destroying it offers a definite military advantage.

Firing rockets from one apartment, or holding hostages in one building, can turn that building into a military objective while that use continues. It does not convert every other home, store, school, hospital, or place of worship into a lawful target. “Those are not civilian infrastructure by every legal definition” is false.

Even after a particular building qualifies as a military objective, the attack can still be a war crime:

You must hit that objective, not treat a whole neighborhood as one target. Treating separated buildings in a populated area as a single military objective is an indiscriminate attack.
Expected civilian deaths and damage to remaining civilian objects cannot be excessive compared with the concrete military advantage.
Hostages and other civilians used as shields stay civilians. Embedding among them is a crime by the defender. It does not cancel distinction, proportionality, or the duty to take feasible precautions.

Some dual-use buildings can be struck. Wholesale leveling of civilian infrastructure does not become legal just because rockets and hostages were present in some of them.

text:
Sri Venugopalaswamy Temple, Karvetinagaram, just 12 km from Puttur and 58 km from Tirupati. Surrounded by gentle hills and lush greenery, the temple offers a serene, picturesque setting that feels like a hidden flute melody in Krishna’s forest.

The only Krishna temple in the Tirupati region, dedicated to Venugopala Swamy. The main deity is carved from a single stone, depicted with a cow behind him and a pot of butter at his feet, flanked by Rukmini and Satyabhama.

Smaller shrines include Rama with Sita, Lakshmana, and Hanuman, Parthasarathy, Renuka Parameshwari, and Avanakshamma. The temple tank is called Skanda Pushkarini.

Built by King Venkataperumal of the Venkataraja dynasty, the temple was once part of the prominent Karvetinagaram Zamindari under the Vijayanagara Empire.

Sarangapani, an 18th-century Telugu poet, composed over 200 padams in praise of Venugopala Swamy here.

text:
Mostly true, with an important caveat about what the court actually did.37
A Cheyenne County ranching family (Dryland Partners / the Dickeys) refused Xcel’s preferred 550-foot route for generation tie-lines connecting two company-owned wind projects (Singing Grass and Cheyenne Ridge II) to the Goose Creek substation. In June 2026, Cheyenne County District Judge Mike Davidson ruled against Xcel: the utility lacked condemnation authority for these lines (they were generation tie-lines, not public transmission serving customers), the taking was not necessary (an alternative route existed), it was not a qualifying public use in this context, and negotiations were in bad faith. Xcel had offered roughly $20,000 after the family had previously sold 90 acres for the substation itself.4
Xcel asked the Colorado Supreme Court to take the case immediately via certiorari, skipping the Court of Appeals, and argued it raised urgent statewide questions about clean-energy interconnection and utilities’ condemnation power. The Colorado Energy Office and Sierra Club filed amicus briefs supporting Xcel. On or about September 1–2, 2026, the Supreme Court issued a brief, unanimous two-paragraph order denying that request. It did not decide the legal merits. Xcel said it will continue its appeal in the Court of Appeals.37
The tweet’s core claims hold: the landowner said no, the district court blocked the taking, the Supreme Court unanimously refused Xcel’s bid to leapfrog and reverse that ruling, and state energy officials plus the Sierra Club had backed Xcel. The phrasing “backed him … over Xcel” is a reasonable popular summary of leaving the landowner’s win in place for now. It is not a final merits ruling that Xcel can never use eminent domain for such lines; that question is still live on appeal. Rocky Mountain Voice’s framing is more polemical than the Colorado Sun reporting it draws from, but the underlying events check out.

text:
In 1989, Pepsi temporarily commanded the 6th largest military navy in the world—and it was all because of vodka.

During the height of the Cold War, Pepsi achieved something no soda company ever had: they broke through the Iron Curtain and became the first capitalist product sold in the Soviet Union.

There was just one massive problem: Soviet rubles were worthless outside the USSR due to strict currency controls.

To pay Pepsi for their syrup, the Soviet government made an unusual deal—they traded Stolichnaya vodka bottle-for-bottle. By the late 1980s, Soviet demand for Pepsi outgrew the global demand for Russian vodka. So, the Soviets offered the only other valuable trade asset they had lying around: decommissioned military hardware.
In 1989, Pepsi signed a deal acquiring 17 submarines, a cruiser, a frigate, and a destroyer. For a brief moment in history, a soft drink company commanded a fleet larger than most national navies. Pepsi’s CEO famously joked to the US National Security Advisor: “We’re disarming the Soviet Union faster than you are.”

What is the most absurd business deal or trade you’ve ever come across in history?

MAYBE YOU’RE NOT LOST… MAYBE YOU’RE ASKING QUESTIONS THAT BELONG TO YOUR OLD LIFE 💫 A DIFFERENT FUTURE REQUIRES DIFFERENT QUESTIONS ✨ SEPTEMBER 3, 2026

Dear friends, sometimes we keep asking life the same questions long after we have become different people. When will this finally happen? Why didn’t that relationship work? When will I know my purpose? How do I get back what I lost? And perhaps the reason some answers never arrive is surprisingly simple: the person you are becoming may no longer need the answers the person you were kept searching for.

What if instead of asking “When will my old dream finally happen?” you asked, “What would excite me now?” Instead of “Why did they leave?” perhaps, “Who am I when I stop waiting for them to return?” Instead of “What am I supposed to do with the rest of my life?” perhaps, “What am I curious enough to explore next?” A new chapter often begins when an old question loses its authority over us.

And this is where September’s 9 frequencies become much more interesting. Completion is not simply clearing people, situations, or memories from our lives. Sometimes what needs to complete is the question itself. We can spend years searching for an answer without noticing that life has already moved us somewhere the question no longer belongs.

The Moon enters Gemini today, bringing movement to our thoughts, conversations, curiosity, and perspective. After the grounding of the last two days, perhaps Divine Intelligence is inviting us to loosen our mental grip and look sideways for a moment. Talk to someone different. Read something unexpected. Follow an unusual idea. Consider the possibility you previously dismissed. Not every message from the Universe arrives as a sign. Sometimes it arrives as a thought that makes you suddenly say, “Wait… what if?”

Our earthly journey will always offer another energetic wave, another alignment, another opening. But none of them are substitutes for living. We are here to participate in the mystery, not simply observe it. To experiment. To love. To choose. To change direction. To discover things about ourselves that no spiritual forecast could reveal in advance. Perhaps curiosity itself is one of the ways Spirit keeps us moving when the old map has reached its edge.

So today, perhaps stop asking life one question you have asked a thousand times. Give the Universe something new to answer. Ask what would make you feel alive again. Ask what you would explore if you weren’t afraid of changing your mind. Ask what becomes possible when the future is no longer required to resemble the past. You don’t need the whole answer today. One different question can be enough to turn your face toward a completely different horizon. And perhaps Divine Presence has been waiting there all along. Have an amazing day. Much love. 💖

WE ARE ONE ♡
Diego E. Berman ©2026

text:
She died in her own home in New York City on Wednesday, September 2, 2026. She was 92 years old. And in the space of one lifetime, she rewrote what it legally meant to be a woman in America.
 Start with 1971, the year before everything changed. An American woman could not walk into a bank and open an account in her own name without complications. She could not apply for a credit card without a husband's signature co-signing the application, as if she were a minor rather than an adult citizen. If a boss cornered her in an office or a supervisor demanded favors for a promotion, there was no law to invoke, because the words "sexual harassment" had not yet been written into any statute. The behavior existed everywhere. The legal language to name it, and to fight it, simply did not.
 That was the world Gloria Steinem set out to dismantle. Not with speeches alone, but with institutions, laws, and a magazine that mainstream publishers said would never survive its first year.
 In 1972, Steinem co-founded Ms. magazine, the first national American publication built, owned, and run entirely by women. Newsstand executives who reviewed the concept predicted it would fold within weeks. The preview issue printed 300,000 copies. It sold out in eight days. Before the month was over, the fledgling magazine had collected 26,000 subscription orders from readers who had never been offered a magazine quite like it before.
 Steinem used that new platform for stories no one else would print. In the spring of 1972, Ms. published a petition called "We Have Had Abortions." Fifty-three prominent American women signed their real names beneath it, publicly admitting to a procedure that was, in most of the country, still a crime. They did it under their own names, months before the Supreme Court would even hear arguments in Roe v. Wade. It was one of the first times American women had collectively broken the public silence around abortion in print, not as a hypothetical or a debate, but as something that had already happened to them.
 She didn't build any of this alone, and never pretended to. Steinem organized across racial lines at a time when the mainstream feminist movement was frequently and fairly criticized for overlooking Black women entirely. She partnered publicly with Dorothy Pitman Hughes, sharing speaking stages with her for years specifically because a white woman and a Black woman standing together made a point neither could make alone. She co-founded the National Women's Political Caucus alongside Florynce Kennedy and Shirley Chisholm, and insisted, in interviews and speeches, that a movement for equality which left out race wasn't a movement for women at all. It was a movement for some women.
 Then she took the fight to Washington. Steinem was among the activists who spent years pushing lawmakers toward what became the Equal Credit Opportunity Act of 1974, the law that finally made it illegal for a bank to require a woman to have a husband, father, or any male relative co-sign before she could get a credit card, a car loan, or a mortgage in her own name. Before 1974, that requirement wasn't an obscure rule buried in fine print somewhere. It was standard banking practice, coast to coast, applied to every adult woman regardless of her income or her credit history.
 Here is what most people miss: none of this was inevitable, and none of it happened quickly. Steinem didn't publish one magazine issue and watch the law change the following year. The credit act took years of testimony and lobbying after Ms. launched. The abortion petition ran roughly nine months before Roe v. Wade was even decided, with no guarantee the Court would rule her way, and no way of knowing whether the fifty-three women who signed it would face professional or legal consequences for doing so. Steinem was building toward outcomes she could not see coming, on a timeline she did not control, using tools that look almost quaint by modern standards: a magazine subscription list, a printed petition, a coalition of women who agreed to disagree constantly about tactics but kept showing up anyway. The slowness is the part that tends to get erased in the retelling. It wasn't a single moment. It was roughly fifty years of unglamorous, incremental work that most of the country wasn't paying attention to while it happened.
 There is a second layer to that, too, and it is the part that makes her story land differently now than it would have a decade ago. Steinem lived long enough to watch parts of what she helped build get legally unwound. In 2022, the U.S. Supreme Court's decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization overturned Roe v. Wade, returning abortion policy to individual states rather than treating it as a nationwide constitutional protection. In the years that followed, numerous state legislatures passed new restrictions on reproductive healthcare, and some school districts and libraries removed books tied to the history she helped write. She watched a constitutional protection that had stood for nearly fifty years get reversed within her own lifetime, decades after she first fought to establish the conditions that made it possible.
 But here is the distinction that mattered most, in the end. A court can overturn a legal precedent. A school board can pull a book off a shelf. A legislature can rewrite a statute. None of those bodies can force an already-working woman to forget how to apply for her own line of credit. None of them can make an office suddenly nameless again, where an employee facing harassment has no word for what happened to her and no law to point to when she reports it. The credit histories already exist. The subscription lists already exist. An entire generation of women who grew up assuming they could open a bank account in their own name already exists, and there is no legislature on earth that can retroactively un-teach that assumption to more than 160 million American women.
 Steinem herself never described any of this as finished business. She said, more than once, that a movement doesn't succeed by winning an argument. It succeeds when the thing it fought for becomes so ordinary that the next generation has to be told it was ever in question at all. That may be the strangest part of her legacy: most American women under 40 have never lived a single day requiring a man's signature to open a bank account, and plenty of them have no idea that fact was ever seriously in dispute. That gap, between the world Steinem was born into in 1934 and the one she died in, at 92, on a Wednesday, in the same city where she built a magazine no one thought would survive its first year, is the real measurement of the life she spent.
 Some people spend a lifetime asking for a seat at the table. She spent hers making sure the table itself could no longer stand without one.

text:
Any political candidate who does not want to call out or deal with Rhode Island’s problems-- problems that were created here in Rhode Island-- is not a serious candidate. Anyone whose messaging centers around national and DC rhetoric instead of the home fires does not deserve your vote.

My focus is on what’s going on right here-- which is why my personal votes will go to the people willing to deal with what’s going on right here. This doesn’t have to be party-partisan. This has to be centered on who’s best for a local job.

Some of the biggest names in the races are more concerned with blaming Washington than blaming the problems that started in Providence. Washington is not responsible for our RI economy, our healthcare crisis, our loss of jobs, the struggles in our education system, the difficulties faced by seniors, our failing infrastructure, or the fact that our state agencies are unable to deliver results. We need to worry about US.

Finger pointing signals a lack of honesty, accountability, and willingness to actually do the job.

If you choose your local candidates based upon national issues, that’s a problem. We need to focus on Rhode Island… and we need honest, decent people willing to do that work. Pay attention to what they tell you, and then believe them. If they say DC is the problem, you can bet your bottom dollar that they are not the solution.

Pay attention to the deep pockets, the campaign ads, and the overall messaging they send. Infighting and attacks are about personal power. They’re never about the people. Is the candidate telling you what they hope to do for you, or are they just telling you why some other guy is bad?

If a candidate has a 30-second ad and all they do is point out their opponent’s flaws, without telling you their own strengths, that probably means they don’t actually have any strengths.

I ran CLEAN campaigns focused on RI because I truly believe that’s the representation I wanted all my life-- and that was the representation I was going to bring. And I’ve lived up to that promise. I don’t win every fight, but I keep showing up with the voice of my constituents.

We need more regular everyday people who are willing to step into the arena and do the hard work. We don’t need more polished finger-pointers. That kind of campaign messaging offers us no solutions, just the same old, same old.

If you want more of the same, go ahead and vote for the people who aren’t willing to grapple with the reality of RI problems, but have tons of cash to blame others. 

BUT, If you truly want change, look for the people who talk about Rhode Island like it matters-- and who tell you what they will do, not just who they will blame.

And remember: endorsements are powerful. An endorsed candidate has allegiances. Many times those allegiances are in the best interest of the people, especially when they’re local. But there are a lot of endorsements out there that are only for the benefit of special interests. Follow the money. Ask whether those allegiances serve us in Rhode Island, or somewhere else.

This is my best advice, folks. You get ONE vote-- spend it like it's your last chip and you're about to lose the house.

Past Tech was historical INNOVATION.

Tech advancement now only serves IMMEDIACY and CONVENIENCE.

There is no INNOVATION in summoning a robot to deliver food ordered from a pocket computer.

There is no INNOVATION in dictating a film premise and receiving an instantly generated script and visuals.

There is no INNOVATION in fleets of autonomous drones conducting perpetual surveillance.

There is no INNOVATION in implanting microchips into healthy human brains to optimize cognition or mood.

There is no INNOVATION in same-day delivery of any material desire.

There is no INNOVATION in vehicles that drive themselves so passengers may remain absorbed in endless digital distraction.

There is no INNOVATION in algorithmic systems engineered to monopolize human attention for commercial gain.

There is no INNOVATION in virtual environments that offer escape from physical reality rather than engagement with it.

There is no INNOVATION in genetic or neural modifications pursued for aesthetic enhancement or convenience rather than the eradication of disease or the expansion of genuine human capability.

text:
Paddy & the 10 pints...

A Texan walks into a pub in Ireland, clears his throat to the crowd of drinkers and says, "I hear you Irish are a bunch of hard drinkers. I'll give 500 American dollars to anybody in here who can drink 10 pints of Guinness back-to-back. "

The room went quiet, and no one took up the Texan's offer. One man, Paddy, even leaves.

Thirty minutes later, the same gentleman who left, Paddy, shows back up and taps the Texan on the shoulder. "Is your bet still good? ", he asks.

The Texan says yes and asks the bartender to line up 10 pints of Guinness.

Immediately, Paddy tears into all 10 of the pints, drinking them all back-to-back. The other pub patrons cheer as the Texan sits in amazement.

The Texan gives the Irishman the $500 and says, "If ya don't mind me askin', where did you go for those 30 minutes you were gone? ".

The Irishman replies, "Oh, I had to go to the pub down the street to see if I could do it first ".

text:
Who Would Have Ever Thought? 

As we start 5787, let’s take stock of the incredible times we live in. In May 1948 a battered remnant of a people declared a state on a sliver of land no one else wanted. Five regular armies crossed its borders within hours. Twenty more governments wished it gone. The Jews inside had no oil, no great-power patron willing to fight for them, almost no heavy weapons, and a fifth column already shooting from behind. The smart money said the experiment would last weeks.

Seventy-eight years later that experiment is a regional power, a technological engine, and the most successful national revival in modern history. The odds were not merely long. They were absurd. That is precisely why the story matters.

The first war was supposed to finish what the Holocaust began. Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Saudia Arabia and Iraq sent trained armies against a militia that had spent the previous decade smuggling rifles in crates of oranges. Inside the new borders, thousands of Arabs took up arms against the government that had just offered them citizenship. The Jews absorbed 6,000 dead, one percent of the entire population, and still held the line. They have not lost a war since. In 1967 they were outnumbered on three fronts and finished the fighting in six days. In 1973 they were surprised, bled, and then drove the attackers back across the canal and the Golan. Every subsequent campaign has followed the same pattern: Israel is smaller, Israel is condemned, Israel survives and wins.

Survival was only the first miracle. The second was the ingathering. Nearly a million Jews fled or were expelled from Iraq, Yemen, Egypt, Libya, Syria and Morocco. They arrived with suitcases and trauma. Then came the remnant of European Jewry, the Soviet aliyah of the 1990s, the Ethiopians, the Indians. Israel did not merely house them. It turned refugees into citizens, conscripts, engineers and rabbis. No other country in the twentieth century absorbed so many people, from so many civilizations, in so short a time, while fighting for its life.

The economic story is almost as improbable. For decades the Arab League enforced a boycott designed to strangle the Jewish state in its crib. Later came the BDS campaign, campus resolutions, and the ritual 69-plus-1 votes at the United Nations, the twenty-two members of the Arab League plus a rotating bloc of forty-eight African and Asian states that treat isolation of Israel as a standing agenda item. Accusations escalated from “occupation” to “apartheid” to “genocide,” language borrowed from the worst crimes of the century and applied to a country that withdraws from territory, accepts cease-fires, and vaccinates its enemies. The intended result was pariah status.

Instead Israel became the Startup Nation. A country with no natural resources except human capital now punches far above its weight in cybersecurity, medical devices, drip irrigation, desalination and semiconductors. Israeli firms list on Nasdaq in numbers that embarrass far larger economies. The same people who once rationed margarine now export intelligence software to governments that once would not stamp an Israeli passport. Poverty has not disappeared, inequality is real, and the cost of living is high. None of that cancels the larger fact: a poor, blockaded state became rich by selling brains.

Diplomacy followed the same improbable arc. The United States, after early hesitation, became Israel’s indispensable ally. That relationship is now so deep that it survives administrations and wars. Meanwhile Israel quietly signed defense and commercial agreements from Colombia to Finland, India to Japan, and, most strikingly, with several Arab states that once led the effort to erase it. The Abraham Accords did not end the conflict. They proved that the old consensus, no recognition until every Palestinian demand is met, was never as solid as its advocates claimed.

The least-noticed success may be the most Jewish. The study halls of Europe were ash. The great yeshivot of Lithuania and Poland existed only in memory and a handful of surviving rabbis. Today Israel houses the largest concentration of full-time Torah scholars in history. The numbers dwarf anything that existed in Vilna or Pressburg. Kollels, women’s seminaries, and community kollelim have multiplied. Chesed networks, food, medical care, burial, mental-health support, operate at a scale the shtetl never imagined. Observance is not uniform; Israel is argumentative by nature. Yet the sheer volume of learning, the density of mitzvah performance, and the public presence of Jewish life exceed anything seen since Sinai, and, in raw numbers of people sitting before open volumes, arguably surpass it. A people that was supposed to vanish rebuilt the very institutions the murderers tried to erase.

None of this was inevitable. It was the product of Divine providence, Jewish resilience,  improvisation, and a refusal to accept the verdict of demographics, geography or the General Assembly. Critics will always list the failures, uncertainty in Gaza, Judea and Samaria that has lasted too long, political divisions, heavy costs of war, the unfinished conflict with the Palestinians. Those criticisms are not imaginary. They simply do not outweigh the central fact. A state that should have died in 1948, or 1967, or 1973, or under the weight of boycotts and resolutions, is still here, still growing, still inventing, still arguing about the meaning of its own existence.

The next seventy-eight years are not guaranteed. Iran’s nuclear program, demographic trends, internal cohesion, mitzvah neglect, and the endurance of Western support all remain open questions. But the record already compiled is not a fluke. It is evidence. Small peoples with a long memory and a short list of alternatives can rewrite the odds. Israel did not merely survive. It turned the most lopsided bet of the twentieth century into a massive success, and, for millions of Jews who had nowhere else to go, into home. That is not a miracle in the sense that it required no human effort. It is a miracle in the only sense that matters: it happened when every reasonable calculation said it would not.

As we start year 5787, let’s be grateful to God for the providential success we’ve enjoyed, the dedication and efforts of our leaders, soldiers, and civil servants who have made this country a success, and commit ourselves to greater Torah observance, dedication to helping our neighbors, and the growth of the Jewish nation.

text:
Lady Death stands as one of the most enduring and fiercely independent figures to emerge from the independent comic book scene of the early 1990s, a pale-skinned goddess of death whose very existence is a monument to betrayal, transformation, and absolute dominion over the end of all things. Created by Brian Pulido and first brought to life through the artwork of Steven Hughes in the pages of Evil Ernie number one from Eternity Comics in December of 1991, she began not as a fully realized character but as the seductive, violent hallucination that haunted the fractured mind of a troubled boy named Ernest Fairchild. That boy would grow into the undead serial killer known as Evil Ernie, and Lady Death was the dark muse who whispered to him of eternal love in exchange for a simple vow to wipe every living soul from the face of the Earth. Over time it became clear she was far more than a figment of a madman’s imagination. She was a genuine demonic entity with her own ancient agenda, and her popularity exploded so thoroughly that she soon claimed her own series and became the flagship character of Chaos Comics, later surviving the company’s collapse to return under Avatar Press and finally under Pulido’s own Coffin Comics imprint where she continues to reign.

The full origin of the woman who became Lady Death reaches back into a brutal medieval European landscape, most often placed in Sweden during an era of crusades and peasant suffering. She was born Hope, the daughter of a cruel nobleman named Matthias, a man who publicly presented himself as a pious Christian warrior waging holy war against pagans yet privately trafficked in black magic, demonology, and the darkest of occult arts. Matthias was a descendant of fallen angels who had once rebelled against Heaven itself, and his bloodline carried that ancient corruption. Hope’s mother, sometimes called Marion or Mary depending on the telling, was a woman of pure and almost heavenly lineage, and her death when Hope was still in her late teens left the girl alone under the tyranny of her father. Matthias conscripted peasants into endless military service and bled the land dry, until the people finally rose in rebellion against him. In the chaos of that uprising he summoned a demon to save his own skin, but Hope was seized by the enraged villagers and accused of witchcraft simply by association with her father’s evil. They dragged her to the stake and prepared to burn her alive.

In that moment of absolute desperation, as the flames began to rise, Hope recalled an incantation she had once overheard her father speak. She uttered the words and a demonic force answered. The entity offered her salvation on the condition that she renounce her humanity forever and pledge herself to the powers of Hell. With no other path left to her, Hope accepted. She was torn from the mortal world and cast into the infernal realms, her skin and hair bleaching to pure white as the mark of her irreversible choice. In Hell she found herself thrust into the middle of a savage civil war between Lucifer, the established Lord of Hell, and a powerful renegade sorcerer who commanded legions of the damned. That sorcerer was her own father, who had already crossed into the netherworld and claimed a place of power there. Gradually the pure girl named Hope was stripped away by the endless violence and corruption that surrounded her. She took the name Lady Death, declaring that the innocent woman she had once been was now dead and gone.

She forged alliances with the outcasts of Hell, most notably an exiled craftsman and blacksmith named Cremator who would become one of her most loyal companions and the forger of her legendary weapons. Under his tutelage and through sheer force of will she learned the arts of war and the arcane energies that now flowed through her transformed body. Lady Death raised an army of the damned and led a full-scale uprising against the Lords of Hell. The final confrontation with Lucifer was apocalyptic. She defeated him in single combat, absorbing portions of his power and casting him through Heaven’s Gate, a place where pure evil cannot endure. In that act she seized the throne of Hell for herself and remade the realm according to her own vision, transforming much of it into the Endless Graveyard, a vast domain of tombs waiting for every soul that must still die so that she might one day walk the Earth again. Lucifer’s dying curse, however, bound her tightly. She could never return to the surface of the mortal world while even a single living being still drew breath. From that moment forward her ultimate goal became the complete extinction of all life on Earth, the only path that would free her from the curse and allow her to reclaim the world of the living.

Across the decades of her published stories Lady Death has endured countless important events that have tested and redefined her. She has used avatars and agents such as Evil Ernie to spread death upon the Earth from afar. She has battled rival demonesses like Purgatori, survived transformations into a darker personality known as Lady Demon, and fought her way through dimension-spanning wars that pitted her against the forces of Heaven, the Chaos Lords, and cosmic entities that predate creation itself. In one era she raised the dead of Valhalla and commanded undead armies against the gods of Asgard. In another she confronted the Horsemen of the Apocalypse and cleaved through legions of angels whose individual power was enough to shatter planets or fly through the hearts of stars. She has been forced into exile, slumbered for decades, awakened to find the world changed, and pursued vengeance against old enemies while discovering she had long-lost children of her own. In the current Coffin Comics continuity she continues to navigate the politics of Hell, defend her throne against pretenders, and edge ever closer to the day when the last living soul falls and the curse is finally broken.

Her powers place her firmly among the higher echelons of superhuman and supernatural beings. Lady Death is functionally immortal, her body sustained by the arcane energies of death itself. She wields vast magical ability that includes necromancy on a scale that allows her to raise and command armies of the undead numbering in the thousands or more, to rip souls from living bodies with a thought, and to reshape entire realms of the afterlife. She can project devastating blasts of hellfire and pure arcane energy, manipulate weather and the elements, transmute matter, create powerful force fields, become intangible, teleport across dimensions, and deliver a death touch that ends life instantly. Physically she possesses strength, speed, durability, and reflexes far beyond human limits, enough to trade blows with fallen angels and cosmic entities. She is a master swordswoman of almost unmatched skill, and the weapons she carries amplify her power to terrifying degrees. The sword Darkness was forged for her by Cremator. Nightmare was created to defeat the Chaos Lord known as Genocide. Apocalypse was shaped from pure chaos and has allowed her to match forces comparable to the Odinpower itself. The Eternal Scythe has slain thousands of powerful angels in a single sweep and cut down beings that required multiple cosmic peers to merely imprison.

In terms of sheer tier she operates at a level that begins at high universe scale in her base form and rises into low multiversal territory when she brings her greatest weapons to bear. She has hurt and defeated Lucifer, the former ruler of Hell. She has bested Genocide, a Chaos Lord who survived the Big Bang and existed in the void before creation. She has matched energies capable of damaging the foundations of reality and has withstood attacks that erased entire sections of Hell. Within the broader landscape of superhero universes this places her well above the vast majority of street-level and mid-tier heroes. Characters such as Batman, Spider-Man, Daredevil, Green Arrow, or even powerhouses like Luke Cage and Iron Man would stand little chance against her raw magical might and death dominion. She outclasses most Asgardian-level threats short of fully empowered Odin or high-end Thor with the Odinforce. Comparisons to Marvel’s Hela are especially favorable to Lady Death; Hela is a powerful goddess of the dead with domain over Hel and the ability to kill with a touch, yet she remains an Asgardian bound by the cosmology of the Nine Realms, whereas Lady Death is a true conqueror of Hell who has personally overthrown its original ruler and rewritten the rules of the afterlife. Mephisto himself, for all his cunning and power, has never demonstrated the same consistent track record of toppling the throne of Hell through direct combat and then holding it against successive waves of cosmic challengers. Lady Death could realistically defeat a great many A-list and even some cosmic-level heroes depending on the circumstances of the fight, particularly those who lack strong resistance to soul manipulation, necromancy, or pure chaos energy. She is not an abstract conceptual force on the level of Marvel’s true Death or DC’s Death of the Endless, beings who embody the end of everything across infinite realities, but within the realm of personal, willful goddesses of death and destruction she ranks among the most dangerous and accomplished.

What makes her story endlessly compelling is the tragic core that never fully disappears beneath the leather, the swords, and the rivers of blood. Somewhere deep inside the pale goddess still carries the memory of the girl named Hope who only wanted to escape the flames and save what little of her family remained. That lingering spark of the mortal she once was gives her moments of unexpected mercy, fierce loyalty to the few she considers true allies, and a relentless drive that has allowed her to survive the collapse of publishing companies, the rewriting of her own continuity, and the passage of more than three decades while remaining one of the most iconic and visually striking anti-heroines the medium has ever produced. She is death made flesh and given agency, a queen who refuses to bow, and a force that continues to reshape the boundaries between the living and the damned with every story that bears her name.

🧵(3/4) 

Subsidiary Iştadevatā

The legend of the goddess Khila Munda and her inclusion in the royal pantheon of Ranpur is very illustrative.

 Once the Rājā of Ranpur was defeated by the Gajapati king. He had to vacate his palace at Ranpur and flee into the deep jungle near the southern border to Banpur. He stayed there, living in distress till Khila Munda, the goddess of this locality, appeared to him in the form of a monkey. While jumping from one tree to another, the monkey did not reach the other tree but returned half way back to the original tree. The Raja of Ranpur understood this as an auspicious sign of the goddess and began to reconquer his state on the same day with the help of the local tribe. Having defeated the troops of the Gajapati, the Raja of Ranpur decided to worship the goddess Khila Munda regularly.

Till today, she occupies the status of a subsidiary istadevată of the Ranpur raj family, next only to the powerful goddess Maninägeśvari. At her place of origin, which can be reached only after several kilometres of walking through the jungle, she is worshipped under big trees in the form of three little carthen heaps of about 15 cm in height, situated near a termite mound. A thatched hut, built a few decades ago, has fallen into a very dilapidated state already. There is no regular pūjā performed, but thrice a month her place is cleaned by her priest Aintha Jani, who also performs sacrifices whenever requested by the local population.

Throughout the year a long bamboo stick (kathi) of about 6 m is kept in the palace compound of Ranpur outside the royal shrine which contains the images of Maninagesvari. This kathi serves as the link between the palace and Khila Munda in the jungle. During Durga Puja, this stick becomes Khila Mundā, or in other words: it becomes the medium of possession in which Khila Munda visits the palace of Ranpur

On the dvitiya oșa day of Durga Puja, Khila Muṇḍā is offered a cock, fish and a bottle of wine at her original place in the jungle by her priest, who keeps a fast. At the same time the Khila Munḍā stick, now adorned with 8 saris (previously 16) is carried by 8 people (previously 16) from the palace in Ranpur to the jungle place of Khila Mundă. After the stick has reached Khila Munda's place in the far-off jungle, the priest, amidst the sound of two big drums (dhola), beaten by two members of the sweeper caste, becomes possessed by the goddess. As the medium (kalisi) of Khiļā Muṇḍā, the priest will then cling to the kathi, which in the meantime has been shouldered by the 8 people from Ranpur. After a few moments, the kalisi suddenly drops on the ground, indicating thus that Khila Munda has now entered the stick

On her way to Ranpur, Khila Munda is worshipped at five places. Near Ranpur she is welcomed by the Jani (non-Brahmin) priest of the Tala Maninägeśvari temple, who also performs a pūjā before her. At the palace itself the worship is taken over and exclusively performed by the royal Brahmin. But the tribal priest receives a sari from the royal storeroom.

After Dasară Khila Mundă returns to her original place in a pigeon, which has been decorated with vermillion and put on the stick. Some feathers found near her shrine are taken as an indicattion that the pigeon died and Khilă Munda returned to her shrine in the jungle

The tutelary goddesses of Baramba

The best example to illustrate this stepwise development of political power & ritual authority is known from the History of the Royal Family of Baramba (Badāmbā rājabanjara itihasa). Baramba, one of the important yet very small Feudatory States has the typical topography of a garhjat (gada jäta = "fort-born") state. Its fort leans with its back against one of the rather low but impenetrable jungle hills still populated by tribals. The palace and the nearby compound of Hindu temples face the fertile & irrigated rice land at the northern bank of the Mahanadi river. Directly at its bank, about 8 km from the fort, at one of Orissa's most beautiful spots, one meets the temple of Bhaṭṭārikā, the "Great Mother" (badamba), from which the state derives its name. According to the Badamba Rajabamsara Itihasa, the legendary founder of Baramba, Haṭakeśvara Raut, met near his future fort a pregnant (garbhābāsa) Saora woman, Sabaruņi. He told her: "I shall cut your head & you will be our thakurani, (we shall) keep your head and worship will be done".

Sabaruņi then told him about the miracles of the place. "This is a piece of land which produces herocs" because a hare wounded a dog and a crane plunged on a falcon.' Hereupon Hatakeśvara asked her again to offer her head and promised to worship her as his family deity. Before offering (samarpita) her head she advised Hatakeśvara to kill one Ramacandra Gaḍatua, a chief of Kharod in the neighbourhood, who was a strong worshipper of the powerful goddess Mahakali. Sabaruni assured him that through worshipping Mahakāli & Bhaṭṭārikā he would become a raja. Hatakeśvara then killed her & kept her head at the gate of his fort. In a slightly different version, the Children's History of Baramba relates that only the fifth Raja of Baramba was able to defeat the chief of Kharod (about 15 km from Baramba) with the secret consent of the goddess Mahākāli who was won over by a tantric Brahmin of Baramba."

During a time of danger it was neither the "martyr-iştadevatā" Sabaruņi nor the subsidiary işṭadevatā Mahākāli who helped the Rājās of Baramba, but the "Great Mother" (baḍamba) Bhaṭṭārikā

Before referring to işṭadevatas of other Garhjat rājās let us have a brief look at the cults of these three tutelary deities of Baramba & their relations with the Rājās of Baramba." Sabaruņi is kept near the entrance of the palace in a small shrine which contains a few small old stone sculptures and two unhewn stones, one of which is worshipped as Sabaruņi. But no regular pūjā is offered to her by the mali priest. Once a year, at Caitra Purnima, she is taken to the nearby hillock Sabaruni Mundia (or Sauruņi Mundamări), a name which may well identify this hillock as the original place of the Sabaruņi worship from where it was transferred to the palace of Baramba. At Caitra Purnima a Sabara sacrifices a male pig by smashing its head. The calanti pratima or "mobile image" of the goddess Bhaṭṭārikā is brought from her shrine in the palace in order to be present during this sacrifice. But neither the rājā nor his räjaguru participates in it. Śabaruņi thus seems to have remained nearly completely a tribal folk deity that had been offered shelter near the palace in recognition of her legendary sacrifice during the establishment of the fort. The yearly sacrifice of a male pig seems to commemorate this primeval human sacrifice. Bhaṭṭārika is likewise known in Odisha for her power (śakti) and her beautiful spot at the Mahanadi. The place must have been associated with human sacrifices and tantrism long before the present temple, displaying typical late medieval Odisha architecture and evading all attempts to determine its exact date, was constructed.

Despite the genuine Hindu architecture of the temple, there is no sculpture of the goddess Instead, a strangely formed piece of the rock, the same on which the temple is constructed, is worshipped in the temple as Bhaṭṭārikā.

The Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) is promoting tuk-tuk travel across Bangkok following the release of LISA’s SaWaDiKa, which takes the familiar Thai greeting and the country’s iconic three-wheeled vehicle to an international audience. TAT, led by Governor Thapanee Kiatphaibool, is encouraging travelers to explore four well-known Bangkok landmarks by tuk-tuk from the afternoon into the night.

The suggested route begins at the Temple of the Emerald Buddha and the Grand Palace in the historic Phra Nakhon district, offering views of traditional Thai architecture and the temple’s distinctive chedis. Travelers can then continue on to the Giant Swing and Wat Suthat, two of Bangkok’s best-known historic sites.

The route continues to the Royal Jubilee Gate at Odeon Circle, regarded as the gateway to Yaowarat, before heading into Bangkok’s Chinatown. After dark, Yaowarat Road offers a contrasting experience with its neon signs, bustling streets, restaurants, and food stalls.

TAT is using the international attention surrounding SaWaDiKa to introduce travelers to different sides of Bangkok, from historic architecture and cultural heritage to street food and nightlife. The route also presents the tuk-tuk as a distinctive way to experience some of the capital’s most recognizable destinations.

text:
🦚💙 KRISHNA JANMASHTAMI 2026 — CELEBRATING THE BIRTH OF LORD KRISHNA

Today, millions of Hindus in India and around the world celebrate Krishna Janmashtami, one of Hinduism’s most joyful and widely celebrated festivals.

If you’re unfamiliar with the festival, here’s the story behind it. 🙏

🦚 WHO IS LORD KRISHNA?

Krishna is one of the most beloved deities in Hinduism and is traditionally regarded as the eighth avatar (incarnation) of Lord Vishnu.

He appears prominently in Hindu sacred traditions and is especially known for his teachings in the Bhagavad Gita, where he speaks about duty, devotion, wisdom and acting without attachment to the rewards of one's actions.

Janmashtami literally celebrates Krishna’s birth — “janma” meaning birth and “ashtami” referring to the eighth lunar day.

📖 THE STORY OF KRISHNA'S BIRTH

According to Hindu tradition, Krishna was born more than 5,000 years ago in Mathura, in northern India.

His parents, Devaki and Vasudeva, had been imprisoned by Devaki’s brother, the tyrannical King Kansa.

A prophecy had warned Kansa that Devaki’s eighth child would bring about his downfall.

Terrified, Kansa imprisoned the couple and killed their children as they were born.

Then came the eighth child — Krishna.

🌙 Tradition says Krishna was born at midnight, while his parents were still imprisoned.

That night, the guards miraculously fell asleep, Vasudeva's chains were released and the prison doors opened.

Vasudeva placed newborn Krishna in a basket and carried him through a storm across the Yamuna River to safety.

He reached Gokul, where Krishna was raised by his foster parents Nanda and Yashoda.

Krishna would eventually defeat Kansa — fulfilling the prophecy.

🌙 WHY IS MIDNIGHT SO IMPORTANT?

Because Krishna is traditionally believed to have been born at midnight, celebrations build throughout the day and reach their emotional peak at 12 AM.

Devotees gather in temples and homes for prayers, devotional songs and readings.

At the symbolic moment of Krishna's birth:

🔔 Temple bells ring
🐚 Conches are sounded
🎶 Devotional songs fill the temples
🙏 Special prayers and aarti are performed
👶 An image of Baby Krishna is ceremonially welcomed

Many devotees fast during the day and break their fast after the midnight worship.

👣 WHY DO SOME HOMES HAVE TINY FOOTPRINTS?

One of the sweetest traditions involves drawing tiny baby footprints from the entrance of the house toward the prayer area.

They represent Baby Krishna entering the home. 💙

Children are also often dressed as little Krishna and Radha, making the festival especially colourful for families.

🧈 WHAT IS DAHI HANDI?

Krishna's childhood stories describe him as mischievous and particularly fond of butter and curd.

He is affectionately remembered as Makhan Chor — “the butter thief.” 😄🧈

According to tradition, when villagers hung pots of dairy products high beyond his reach, Krishna and his friends would work together to reach them.

That story inspired Dahi Handi.

In places such as Maharashtra, teams form spectacular human pyramids to reach and break an earthen pot suspended high above the ground.

It turns an ancient childhood story into a celebration of teamwork, courage and joy.

🎭 HOW ELSE IS JANMASHTAMI CELEBRATED?

Celebrations vary beautifully across India.

🛕 Temples are decorated with flowers and lights
🎶 Bhajans and kirtans — devotional songs — continue late into the night
🎭 Ras Leela/Krishna Leela performances recreate episodes from Krishna's life
👶 Baby Krishna idols are placed in decorated cradles
🧈 Butter, sweets and other foods are offered to Krishna
🙏 Families pray, fast and later share prasad — food that has been offered during worship

Mathura, Krishna's traditional birthplace, and nearby Vrindavan, associated with his childhood, become major centres of celebration, drawing devotees from around the world.

🌏 MORE THAN A BIRTHDAY

For devotees, Janmashtami isn't simply remembering the birth of a deity.

Krishna's story represents the belief that righteousness can ultimately overcome injustice, wisdom can overcome confusion, and divine love can overcome fear.

From a midnight birth in Mathura…

to temples and homes across the world…

the story of Krishna continues to bring millions together in faith, music, colour and joy. 🦚💙

🙏 Happy Krishna Janmashtami!

Jai Shri Krishna!

text:
Cracks in Foundation of Traditionis Custodes
Previously undisclosed documents raised serious questions about the stated rationale for Pope Francis’ 2021 decree restricting the Traditional Latin Mass. Diane Montagna
(Abridged by Robert t. Fertig with some Vital viewpoints.)
This journalist has obtained the Vatican’s overall assessment of the consultation of bishops that have “prompted” Pope Francis to Revoke Summorum Pontificum, Pope Benedict XVI’s 2007 letter liberalizing the “Traditional Latin Mass” and Sacraments.
July 1, 2025-- New evidence exposes major cracks in the foundation of Traditionis Custodes, Pope Francis’ 2021 decree that significantly restricted the Traditional Roman liturgy. “The majority of bishops who responded to the questionnaire stated that making changes to Summorum Pontificum would cause more harm than good.”
The assessment contradicts rationale for imposing Traditionis Custodes, and raises serious questions about its credibility.
When, on July 16, 2021, Pope Francis promulgated Traditionis Custodes, he said responses to the questionnaire “reveal a situation that preoccupies and saddens me and persuades me of the need to intervene.”
Viewpoint: This was a “totally false claim” by the late Pope Francis. Unfortunately, Pope Leo XIV continues this deceitful situation. This excellent report by Diane Montagna, from Rome, makes it clear to me these past fabrications to thousands of bishops and millions of Traditional Catholics has continued to this date with Pope Leo.
Diane Montagna: “Regrettably,” [Francis] said to the world’s bishops, “the pastoral objective of my Predecessors … has often been seriously disregarded. An opportunity offered by St. John Paul II and, with even greater magnanimity, by Benedict XVI … was exploited to widen the gaps, reinforce the divergences, and encourage disagreements that injure the Church, block her path, expose her to the peril of division.”
[Pope Francis] told the bishops that he was “constrained” by their “requests” to revoke not only Summorum Pontificum but all the norms, instructions, permissions and customs” that preceded his new decree.”
However, the Vatican’s overall assessment reveals is that the “gaps”, “divergences”, and “disagreements” stem more from a level of nescience, prejudice and resistance of “a minority (not a majority) of bishops to Summorum Pontificum” than from any problems originating from adherents to the traditional Roman liturgy.
Conversely, the official CDF report states, “the majority of bishops responding to the questionnaire, who have generously and intelligently implemented Summorum Pontificum, ultimately express satisfaction with it.” [In addition,] “in places where the clergy have cooperated with the bishop, the situation has become completely pacified.”
The assessment confirms the contention reported by Montagna in October 2021: That Traditionis Custodes magnified and projected as a major problem what was ancillary in the official CDF report.
Viewpoint: The text shows that Traditionis Custodes disregarded and withheld what the report said about the peace Summorum Pontificum had restored, and turned a blind eye to “constant observation made by the bishops” that younger people were drawn to the Catholic Church through this older form of the liturgy.
Genesis and Structure of the Official Report
The task of preparing the official report was entrusted to the Fourth Section of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith. Until TC, this entity, formerly known as the Pontifical Ecclesia Dei Commission, was responsible for supervising the observance and application of the provisions established in Summorum Pontificum. Consequently, the Fourth Section possessed a breadth of experience and expertise with which to view and analyze the survey results.
In the spring of 2020, CDF Prefect Cardinal Luis Ladaria sent the questionnaire to the presidents of episcopal conferences worldwide, for distribution to diocesan bishops. The responses were time-honored by the CDF until January 2021. The Fourth Section processed and analyzed the body of material submitted.
While Montagna has not seen the report in its entirety, she learned that the 224-page final report, dated February 2021, comprises two main parts. The First Part offers a detailed analysis of the survey results and findings continent-by-continent, and country-by- country, including charts and graphs illustrating data and trends.
The Second Part, titled “Summary” includes an introduction, a summary on each continent, an Overall Assessment of the survey results, and a collection of quotations drawn from the responses received from the dioceses. This collection was to provide Pope Francis with a representative sampling of the bishops’ responses.
The overall assessment noted that Summorum Pontificum played “a significant, albeit relatively modest, role in the life of the Church.” By 2021, “it had spread to about 20% of the Latin dioceses worldwide, and its enactment was “more serene and peaceful. …”
Viewpoint: Pope Francis falsely stated in Traditionis Custodes that he “considered the wishes expressed by the episcopate and heard the opinion of the Congregation for the Doctrine of Faith.” The overall assessment is precisely the part of the report that synthesizes and interprets the survey results, offering an evaluative conclusion drawn from the evidence. It reflects the informed judgment of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith. Francis not only had the report, but literally snatched a working copy out of Cardinal Ladaria’s hands during an audience, telling him he wanted it immediately because he was curious about it.
The Vatican never released the full contents of the official report, in October 2021 Diana Montagna obtained and published the collection of quotations included in Part II—indicating only the country or region from where the quotations originated.
The Overall Assessment. Seven Key Points:
1. Lack of liturgical peace and unity is due more to the minority of bishops than to adherents of the Traditional Roman Liturgy.
Where liturgical peace is lacking, the report shows it stems more from a level of nescience, prejudice and resistance of a minority of bishops to Summorum Pontificum than from any problems originating from those drawn to the Traditional Roman Liturgy.
The CDF report recalls Benedict XVI’s desire to achieve, through the implementation of Summorum Pontificum, an “internal liturgical reconciliation” within the Church, and his recognition of the need “to proceed not according to a hermeneutic of rupture but rather by renewal in continuity with tradition.”
“This ecclesiological dimension of the hermeneutic of continuity with tradition and with a coherent renewal and development has not yet been fully embraced by some bishops,” the report observes. “However, where it has been received and implemented, it is already bearing fruit, the most visible, which is in the [traditional] liturgy.”
Furthermore, the report laments that “in some dioceses the Forma extraordinaria [Extraordinary Form] is not considered a richness for the life of the Church, but rather as an inappropriate, disturbing, and useless element for ordinary pastoral life, and even as ‘dangerous’ and therefore something not to be granted, or to be suppressed, or at least strictly controlled so that it does not spread, in the hope of its eventual disappearance or abrogation.”
More specifically, the report found that bishops in Spanish-speaking regions generally “seem to show little interest” in Summorum Pontificum, despite requests from the faithful.Similarly, it noted, “the responses from Italian bishops suggest that they do not hold the Forma extraordinaria and its related provisions in high regard.”
Regarding a misunderstanding or ignorance among a minority of the episcopate, the report noted: “Some bishops state that the Summorum Pontificum has failed in its aim of fostering reconciliation and therefore request its suppression—either because internal reconciliation within the Church has not yet been fully achieved, or because the Priestly Fraternity of St. Pius X has not returned to full communion with the Church.” In response, the authors observe that the process of reconciliation in the Church is often “slow and gradual,” and they recall, as Benedict XVI himself did, that Summorum Pontificum was not intended for the SSPX.
Additionally, some bishops fear a “division into two Churches” and believe that groups attached to the Extraordinary Form “reject” the Second Vatican Council. The report acknowledges that the latter point is “partly true” but says that it “cannot be generalized”. It adds, “Bishop’s pastoral care has been decisive in calming agitated spirits and clarifying the thinking of members of the stable groups.”
2. Majority of bishops who implemented Summorum Pontificum expressed satisfaction with it.
Conversely, the report found that “the majority of bishops who responded to the questionnaire, and who have implemented the Summorum Pontificum, ultimately express satisfaction with it.” It adds, "In places where the clergy have closely cooperated with the bishop, the situation has become completely pacified.”
The report found that “Bishops most attuned to this matter observe that the older form of the liturgy is a treasure of the Church to be safeguarded and preserved: it constitutes good to find unity with the past, to know how to advance along a path of coherent development and, and to meet, as far as possible, the needs of these faithful.”
According to the report: “The majority of bishops who responded to the questionnaire state that making legislative changes to the MP Summorum Pontificum would cause more harm than good.”
Based on its findings, the report predicts, “Weakening or suppressing Summorum Pontificum would seriously damage the life of the Church, as it would recreate tensions that the document had helped to resolve.”
Some bishops thought a legislative change to Summorum Pontificum would “foster the departure of disappointed faithful from the Church toward the Society of St. Pius X or other schismatic groups”, foster distrust toward Rome, give rise to “a resurgence of the liturgical wars” and “the emergence of schisms.” Moreover, “it would delegitimize two Pontiffs—John Paul II and Benedict XVI—who had committed themselves to not abandoning these faithful.”
3. Bishops are grateful for the competence of the CDF Fourth Section (the disbanded Pontifical Commission Ecclesia Dei)
The report stressed the importance of stable groups and communities having a “competent interlocutor” at the institutional level, i.e. at the Holy See. The report notes that careful oversight carried out by those with experience and expertise helps to “prevent arbitrary forms of self-management and anarchy within the groups, as well as abuses of power by some local bishops.”
4. Report confirms the attraction of youth to Traditional liturgy.
The CDF report confirmed Pope Benedict’s intuition, expressed in Summorum Pontificum that younger people would find in the traditional Roman liturgy “a form of encounter with the mystery of the Holy Eucharistic particularly suited to them.”
“A constant observation made by the bishops is that it is young people who are discovering and choosing this older form of the liturgy. The majority of the stable groups present in the Catholic world are composed of young people, often converts to the Catholic faith or those returning after a time away from the Church and the sacraments. They are drawn by the sacredness, seriousness, and solemnity of the liturgy. What strikes them most, also amid a society that is excessively noisy and verbose, is the rediscovery of silence within sacred actions, the restrained and essential words, preaching that is faithful to the Church’s doctrine, the beauty of liturgical chant, and the dignity of the celebration: a seamless whole that is deeply attractive.”
5. Report highlighted growth of vocations in Ex-Ecclesia Dei communities since Summorum Pontificum.
The CDF report highlighted the growth in vocations in former Ecclesia Dei communities since the promulgation of Summorum Pontificum but noted that some diocesan bishops are not pleased by this. “Many young men,” it said, “are choosing to enter the Ecclesia Dei institutes for their priestly or religious formation rather than diocesan seminaries, to the regret of some bishops…”
6. Report recommended studying both forms of Roman Rite as part of seminary formation.
The report therefore suggested, based on an idea proposed by bishops, that “sessions dedicated to the study of both forms of the Roman Rite” be incorporated into seminary formation and other ecclesiastical faculties, as a means of fostering greater unity and peace, increasing diocesan vocations, and preparing “suitably formed priests” for celebrating the Roman Rite.
7. The report recommends, “Let the people be free to choose.”
Based on the findings of the survey of the episcopate, and citing a Filipino bishop, the CDF report concludes by recommending: “Let the people be free to choose.” Recalling Bishop’s irreplaceable, albeit sometimes challenging, role and duty before God to tend the flock, the report ends with Pope Benedict XVI’s words to the Bishops of France in 2008, concerning Summorum Pontificum:
“I am aware of your difficulties, but I do not doubt that, within a reasonable time, you can find solutions satisfactory for all, lest the seamless tunic of Christ be further torn. Everyone has a place in the Church. Every person, without exception, should be able to feel at home, and never rejected. God, who loves all men and women and wishes none to be lost, entrusts us with this mission by appointing us shepherds of his sheep. We can only thank him for the honor and the trust that he has placed in us. Let us therefore strive always to be servants of unity.”
Guardians of Tradition?
This assessment becomes known after the Archdiocese of Detroit became the latest to suffer from a crackdown by the Vatican’s Dicastery for Divine Worship and the Discipline of the Sacraments (DDW), the dicastery charged with enforcing Traditionis Custodes.
In April, its newly installed Archbishop announced that the Traditional Latin Mass [is] no longer permitted in parish churches as of July 1, 2025. Citing a 2023 Vatican rescript from DDW prefect Cardinal Arthur Roche, the archbishop informed priests “local bishops no longer possess the ability to permit the older form of the liturgy in a parish.” [This tyrant Archbishop fired two excellent professors, who taught seminarians’ for 20-years, without cause.]
In his response to the final question of the Vatican survey, which Montagna has obtained, former Archbishop of Detroit, Allen Vigneron, summed up what—according to the official report—the majority of bishops had actually requested. The survey asked, “Thirteen years after the motu proprio Summorum Pontificum, what is your advice about the Extraordinary Form of the Roman Rite?” Archbishop Vigneron replied:
“My advice is to maintain the discipline and norms set out in Summorum Pontificum, and to deal with any problems that are arising by calling priests and people to observe them. The motu proprio has given us a remarkably successful approach to resolving the contention that existed in the Church about the status of the Extraordinary Form. The discipline it has put in place is bearing much good fruit, especially in the lives of the faithful and in restoring ecclesial peace. There is no question in my mind about the legitimacy of the Extraordinary Form as extraordinary. These celebrations offer valid experiences of the Church’s sacred liturgy but complement the Ordinary Form. Such celebrations are in no way a threat to the Ordinary Form established after the Council, and in the Church, they enrich her in her diversity. By my lights Summorum Pontificum has been a remarkable success.”
The moral justification of Traditionis Custodes was always weak given the positive fruits that have come from the Traditional Roman Rite, its growing popularity, especially among the young, its influence on the family as the “domestic church,” and its ability to attract vocations. This new discovery of the CDF’s overall assessment of its consultation of bishops concerning Summorum Pontificum serves to cast further doubts on the foundation and credibility of Traditionis Custodes.
Viewpoint: This observer will not compromise with the actual truth.  Popes, Francis and Leo, have spread false survey results to thousands of Bishops and millions of Catholics, worldwide to support their Modernistic objectives. As the Church marked the 60th anniversary of the close of the Second Vatican Council, a quotation from Pope Paul VI — “… the smoke of Satan has entered the temple of God” — began circulating widely online.
The line, drawn from Pope Paul VI 1972 homily, is a frank admission that Vatican II was a big mistake — that in the years following the council, evil forces bent on destroying her from within had subverted the Church. In this reading, “the temple of God” refers to the Vatican; the “smoke of Satan” to corrupt or heretical bishops; and the “fissure” (sometimes translated as “crack”) to the modernizing reforms of Vatican II.

text:
Navagio Shipwreck: Zakynthos at Its Most Dramatic

There are beautiful beaches, and then there are places that seem almost designed for a movie.

Navagio, often called Shipwreck Beach, is one of the most recognisable landscapes in Greece. A weathered shipwreck rests on the white beach while enormous pale cliffs rise dramatically around the bay.

The contrast is extraordinary.
The famous scene combines:
• Bright white sand
• Deep turquoise Ionian water
• Towering limestone cliffs
• The iconic shipwreck
• Dramatic coastal scenery

The journey to Navagio has traditionally been part of the experience, with boat trips approaching the spectacular coastline from the sea.

From the water, the scale of the cliffs becomes immediately obvious. Their pale rock contrasts beautifully with the intense blue of the Ionian Sea.

The famous viewpoint above the beach offers a completely different perspective, revealing the shape of the bay and explaining why this location became one of Greece's most photographed sights.

Navagio has also become a symbol of Zakynthos itself, appearing on postcards, travel brochures and social media feeds around the world.

But there is more to the experience than taking the perfect photograph.

Look at the cliffs. Watch the colour of the water change with the sunlight. Notice how tiny the boats look against the landscape.

And remember that access and swimming conditions can vary, so always check current local restrictions before planning a visit.

Navagio is spectacular because it feels almost unreal.

White sand. Blue water. Giant cliffs. A shipwreck in the middle of it all.

Sometimes Greece really does look like Greece.

text:
Scientists just successfully reversed cognitive decline and brain damage in Alzheimer's mice.

Traditionally, Alzheimer’s disease has been considered an irreversible condition, with existing treatments only slowing down its devastating progression. However, a groundbreaking study from researchers at the University of South Carolina has shattered this paradigm. 

Using a novel polymer nanogel system called "Nano-ERASER," the team managed to cross the blood-brain barrier and target astrocytes—star-shaped support cells in the central nervous system. By delivering antibodies that break down the PTBP1 protein, the treatment successfully prompted these support cells to transform into fully functional, mature neurons. 

This innovative cellular reprogramming occurred without modifying the genetic code, representing a safer, non-permanent alternative to traditional gene editing.

The results in animal models were nothing short of remarkable. After receiving just two intravenous injections, mice modeled with advanced Alzheimer’s disease demonstrated dramatic cognitive recovery, successfully regaining their ability to navigate complex water mazes and build nests. Beyond behavioral improvements, brain analyses revealed a significant increase in neuron density, a reduction in toxic amyloid-beta protein plaques, and a marked decrease in neuroinflammation. While the transition from animal models to human clinical trials will require years of rigorous safety testing, this study offers an inspiring proof of principle that the damaged adult brain can indeed be regenerated.

source: Wang, M., Wang, J., Wang, Y., Raja, M. K., Gupta, G., Hu, X., Shi, S., Chen, H., Fan, D., & Xu, P. (2026). Reverse the progression of Alzheimer's disease through Nano-ERASER-based adult neuroregeneration. Cell Biomaterials.

Tariff Advantage Must for Bilateral Trade Agreement with US: Goyal

India's Firm Stand
India holding out for a clear tariff advantage over its competitors in the US market before signing off on the proposed Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) with Washington

Commerce & Industry Minister Piyush Goyal: India will finalise the BTA only after the US offers preferential tariff rates compared with competing economies

"As soon as the US is able to give us the preferential rate in comparison to our competition, we will finalise the BTA and announce the final details"

Absolute tariff number should not be viewed in isolation — India's position relative to competing countries matters more

The Competition
India competes in the American market with Vietnam, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Cambodia — all negotiating their own agreements with the US

India faced a 25% reciprocal tariff plus a separate 25% levy linked to Russian oil purchases

US Supreme Court struck down the reciprocal tariffs — Washington subsequently imposed a uniform 10% tariff under an emergency provision of the Trade Act

Those tariffs expiring on June 24 and being replaced by Section 301 duties targeting forced-labour-linked imports

Current FTA Landscape
India has implemented FTAs with UK, Mauritius, Oman, UAE and Australia

Agreement with New Zealand expected to become operational soon

Trade pact with 27-nation EU also expected to follow

India had secured a tariff advantage in the February framework for an interim trade deal — when the US was imposing different reciprocal tariffs on trading partners

BHAVYA Industrial Parks
Exporters to receive priority support in the proposed 100 BHAVYA industrial parks

Concessions for companies committing to higher export levels

Access to plug-and-play infrastructure

Broader Trade Agreements
Agreements being pursued with Canada, Mexico, Chile, Mercosur, SACU, GCC and Israel

Along with reviews of trade arrangements with ASEAN, South Korea and Japan

Could eventually give Indian exporters preferential access covering about 75% of global trade

Word of Caution
Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal warned that preferential access secured through FTAs would not remain a permanent advantage — India's competitors would eventually negotiate similar agreements

India trades across around 12,300 tariff lines — most covered in some form by its trade agreements

Exporters have a five-to-10-year window to build new supply chains and exploit the market access created by FTAs

text:
If I were recruiting the first 10 employees for a startup, this is how I'd approach it.

First, I wouldn't start by asking:

"Who do we want to hire?"

I'd ask:

"What problems do we need these people to solve?"

Because every startup is different.

A fintech, SaaS company, e-commerce startup and health-tech company won't necessarily need the same first 10 employees.

Here's my approach:

1. Identify the critical functions:
What must be done for the business to operate and grow?

2. Define each role clearly:
Responsibilities, required skills, experience level, reporting line, compensation and what success looks like.

3. Prioritize the hires:
Not every position needs to be filled at the same time. I'd identify the roles that have the biggest immediate impact.

4. Create a candidate profile for each role:
What does the ideal candidate actually need to be able to do?

5. Source strategically:
I'd combine job platforms, LinkedIn, professional communities, referrals and targeted outreach rather than simply posting and waiting.

6. Screen before interviewing:
The goal isn't to interview everyone who applies. I'd shortlist candidates based on the actual requirements of the role.

7. Use structured interviews:
Every candidate should be assessed against relevant criteria, not just whether the interviewer “likes their vibe.”

8. Assess practical ability where necessary.
For certain roles, a relevant task or work sample can provide useful evidence of capability.

9. Make decisions based on evidence:
Skills, experience, potential, role requirements and overall suitability, not desperation to fill the vacancy.

10. Don't stop at the offer letter:
I'd make sure there's a proper onboarding process so the new hire understands the company, their responsibilities and what is expected of them.

And one more thing:
I wouldn't necessarily recruit all 10 people at once.

A startup should hire based on its actual stage, priorities and resources.

The goal isn't to have 10 employees.

The goal is to have the right people solving the right problems at the right time.

That's what good startup recruitment should look like.

text:
Getting hired as a remote worker is one thing. Staying valuable enough that your Client wants to keep you is another.

When you work remotely, your manager doesn’t see everything you do throughout the day.

What they do see is how you communicate, how reliable you are, how you handle problems, and whether you follow through on your work.

Over time, those things shape how much they trust you.

Here are 16 traits that can make you a truly valuable remote worker:

1. Focus on the work, not the spotlight: You do not need to constantly prove you are working. Let your results speak.

2. Help others succeed without seeking credit: Great teammates understand that another person’s success does not reduce theirs.

3. Anticipate problems: Do not wait until something breaks. Spot potential issues early and act.

4. Bring solutions, not just problems: Instead of saying, “There’s an issue,” try, “Here’s the issue and here’s what I suggest we do.”

5. Keep your promises: If you say you will deliver on Friday, deliver on Friday. Reliability builds trust.

6. Prioritize progress over perfection: Remote work moves quickly. Learn to produce quality work without getting trapped in endless perfectionism.

7. Communicate clearly: Your teammates cannot read your mind. Give clear updates, ask clear questions, and communicate delays early.

8. Stay calm under pressure: Things will go wrong. The person who can think clearly when everyone else is panicking becomes incredibly valuable.

9. Adapt quickly: New tools. New systems. New priorities. Remote workers who can adjust without constant resistance are easier to work with.

10. Protect your time respectfully: Being available 24/7 does not make you a better remote worker. Learn to set healthy, professional boundaries.

11. Collaborate instead of competing: Remote teams need people who share information, support colleagues, and work toward the same goal.

12. Listen more than you speak: Good communication is not just about expressing yourself. It is also about understanding what others actually need.

13. Lift others up: Share knowledge. Encourage your teammates. Celebrate their wins.

14. Simplify complexity: If you can take a complicated process and make it easier to understand or execute, you are extremely valuable.

15. Offer quiet support: Not every contribution needs an announcement. Sometimes the most valuable teammate is the one who simply notices what needs to be done and helps.

16. Keep your ego in check: Be willing to learn, accept feedback, admit mistakes, and change your approach when necessary.

The biggest lesson?

Remote work is not just about being good at your job.
It is about becoming someone people can trust to do the job well, communicate effectively, solve problems, and make the team better.

Skills can make you employable.
Reliability, communication, ownership, and collaboration can make you indispensable.

If you are building a career as a remote worker, save this list and use it as a personal checklist.

Which of these traits are you currently working on?
