"So that’s the story. He apologized.

I listened to what he said. The question is what he thinks he apologized for.

After the attack on Temple Israel in West Bloomfield, El-Sayed condemned it. Then he kept going. “Hurt people hurt people.” He brought up the attacker’s family, killed in an Israeli airstrike in Lebanon, and the “cycle” of violence. Jewish children had just been targeted at a synagogue in Michigan. He wanted the room to hear about the terrorist’s pain, too.

Jewish Democrats in the state were among the people who were furious. Now he’s the nominee in a race that could decide the Senate, and those comments are a problem. Hence the apology tour.

To reporters: “My comments might have been misconstrued to be justifying something I did not intend to justify.” Then: “To anybody who feels like my comments might have been hurtful, I’m really sorry. That was not my intention.”

Misconstrued. Anybody who feels. Not my intention.

He has also said, “I made a mistake,” and told Jewish Democrats the first condemnation should have ended there. “Full stop.”

Then he told you what the mistake was.

“What I was trying to do is offer context for why it happened. But it wasn’t the time for context.”

He still thinks the context belonged. He put it this way: “When you give the right medicine at the wrong time, it’s the wrong medicine and I gave it at the wrong time.”

Right medicine.

That line should be in the stories. He still treats the terrorist’s grievance against Israel as the correct analysis of an attack on Jewish kids. He just thinks he said it too soon.

JTA noticed. After his meetings with Jewish Democrats, it reported that in both spoken apologies he “insisted the main problem was with the timing of his attempt to apply ‘context’ to the situation, not with the substance of what he said.”

That’s the part the “EL-SAYED APOLOGIZES” headlines bury."

What explains people like Michigan AG Dana Nessel? 
Internalized stigma.
Members of stigmatized groups often adopt the majority's frame of reference, including its negative valuation of the in-group. If the surrounding culture treats your particularity as the problem, aligning with the universal that condemns it, is a route to belonging, safety, and status.

Universalism as an exit from vulnerability.
For a small, historically persecuted people, particularist self-defense is materially precarious. Universalism — cosmopolitanism, socialism, human-rights discourse — offers a frame in which the Jewish problem dissolves because the categories themselves dissolve. The "non-Jewish Jew” is not self-hating so much as invested in a horizon where the distinction no longer signifies.

In-group differentiation under threat.
Social identity theory has a lot to say about why some minority members respond to group-directed hostility by distancing from the group ("I'm not one of those Jews") rather than by embracing it. It's a survival strategy, and it's especially available to the assimilated and the elite.

text:
Ch. 6 of NITRO: The Inside Story of WCW Monday Nitro's Debut - 31 Years Ago Today (9/4/95)!   

If Luger couldn’t keep quiet, word of his possible ‘jump’ would surely reach the WWF. Although Nitro would emanate as a live program, secretive plans leaked frequently in wrestling, spawning a humorous expression in the process: telephone, telegram, tell-a-wrestler…  

Such disclosures were often reported by the wrestling media, a collection of newsletters, magazines and radio shows that @EBischoff mostly loathed. “I had absolutely no respect for them,” he says, “nor did I value their opinions at all. There was no reason to, quite frankly.”    

On Monday, August 14th, 1995, WCW organized a press event for ‘legitimate’ media members - the formal launch of Monday Nitro. At a press conference held at the Harley Davidson Cafe in New York - for all intents and purposes, the WWF’s backyard - Brad Siegel valiantly professed that WCW was an ideal fit for his network. “We actually went to WCW and said, ‘we want a show that will be the best wrestling event on television, and we wanna put it on Monday nights’,” the network president claimed.    

Strategically, TNT selected a start date for Nitro to air unopposed; in other words, without competition, as in a fortuitous occurrence, Raw was set to be pre-empted by the U.S. Open, leaving the entire wrestling audience up for grabs (for one week, at least).    

“We’d like to make an announcement today that I’m very, very pleased to make,” continued Siegel. “Starting Labor Day night - Monday September 4th - TNT will once again live up to its name in a very explosive way. WCW wrestling comes to our network, live every week, in prime time and from a different city.”    

“WCW Monday Nitro Live! will be seen Monday nights live at 9pm Eastern, and will originate - as we said - from a different city, every single week. The one hour telecast will be replayed at midnight Eastern, nine o’clock Pacific, [and] WCW’s debut on TNT will be live from the Mall of America in Minneapolis, Minnesota. [It] will be called the ‘Brawl at the Mall’.”    

The choice of venue for the first show was, in the eyes of many wrestling purists, an unusual one. But located near the Minneapolis-Saint Paul metropolitan area, the 4.2 million sq. ft. Mall would provide a glittering backdrop for the spectacle - and with over 30,000 daily visitors to the plaza, a curious and suitably large crowd for the show could be expected. Interestingly, the Mall became a viable idea only after initial discussions regarding a New York City debut were swiftly thwarted, the consequence of the WWF’s exclusivity agreement with Madison Square Garden. “There are a lot of interesting things in the business of booking arenas,” smirked Bischoff, standing confidently at the press podium. “We will come from New York [in the future],” he promised.    

“WCW wrestling will become the centerpiece of a brand new franchise on TNT called Monday Nitro,” continued Siegel. “Each week at eight o’clock - leading in to the telecast - we will present the action adventure television series Thunder in Paradise which stars Hulk Hogan. After both airings of WCW on TNT, we will present a very heavy duty action movie to make Monday Nitro a very action-driven night [of television].    

“TNT is becoming known for a network that has the best of its kind. We’ve got the best sports franchises with the NFL and the NBA. We’re quickly becoming the best maker of original movies on TV....we have the best cartoons...the best movie library available. [And so] we thought it was about time to put the best wrestling on TNT.”   

“It’s a heck of an opportunity,” beamed Bischoff in support several minutes later. “Those of you who...have watched our growth over the last 12 months know that there’s a lot of momentum here. I wanna thank Brad. I wanna thank everybody at TNT.    

“There’s a lot of great people [working at TNT]. They’re creative. They’re driven. They’re aggressive...and that’s the kind of combination we felt we needed to take WCW to the next level. And that’s exactly what we intend to do.”    

As the press conference wore on, a stoic Siegel witnessed a buoyant Bischoff boldly predict a competitive ratings battle from the start. “Since the addition of Hulk Hogan and Randy Savage, [WCW] has really closed the gap [with the WWF],” argued Bischoff. “We’re coming on strong and we have a lot of momentum. We believe that we’ve got the biggest stars in our industry...and that’s what entertainment is all about. [People are] entertained by stars, and we’ve got ‘em in WCW. Now [fans are] going to have a choice. They can watch whatever else is going on...or they can flip on over and watch Monday Nitro on TNT.    

“This show is gonna be in your face...up to the edge...over the edge...[there’s gonna be a] surprise every single Monday. It’s gonna be live and when I tell you it’s ‘in your face’, I mean it’s gonna be in your face...this is an incredibly different product.    

“I think the fact that we have the biggest stars in the industry already differentiates us from the WWF and Monday Night Raw. A lot of the people they have over there are kind of...WCW has-beens. We’re gonna be live every week - they’re not. We’re gonna take the show all over the country.    

“All I can say is tune in. September 4th, you’ll see the difference. I can stand up here and talk all afternoon long about creatively, all of the different things that we’re gonna do…but we’re gonna give the show an edge. This show is gonna be more like rock-and-roll than meat and potatoes. [It’s a] faster pace, more of an MTV-type of show.    

“[So] how long do I think it’s gonna take [to become number one]? Hey, I’m not gonna [instantly] overtake a company that’s done a pretty good job of branding themselves in this position for the last couple of years. This is a long-term project for us. We’re not doing this to just see if it’s gonna work for six months. This is a long-term project, and we’ve got a big commitment from the Turner organization, Brad Siegel, and some very aggressive creative people over at TNT.    “The only thing I like better than competition is winning, and we look forward to [winning].”    

But it would not be Bischoff, however, who would deliver the most biting comment in the WWF’s direction. Mindful of the potential impact of a Lex Luger defection, Sting - representing the stars of WCW along with Hulk Hogan and Randy Savage - presciently foreshadowed what was about to come.  “All I gotta say to sum it up,” Sting bellowed at the media, “[is] somebody is in for a Raw deal.”  
__________________________   

Returning to the New York market in his red-and-yellow garb, Hulk Hogan generated significant attention at the press conference. Showcasing the affable charm that long endeared him to decision makers - both in and out of the industry - since the early 1980s, Hogan took to the podium with ease. “Now I’ve got Mr. Siegel right where I want him,” he joked, demonstrating a headlock before teasing an eventual match with Savage, almost in the very next breath. After a deft Harley Davidson plug, Hogan prepared to conclude his comments with a modification of a catch phrase he made famous in an earlier time. “What are you gonna do,” he asked rhetorically, “when Hulk Hogan and Monday Nitro run wild on you?”    

Curiously, the line was delivered, but devoid of reaction. Hogan’s eyes darted as he repeated himself, fighting back against an apparent glitch in the matrix. “What are you gonna do when Hulk Hogan and Monday Nitro run wild on you?” he demanded again, achieving some mild applause in response. For the first time in a long time - maybe forever - the usually willing media greeted the Hulkster routine with a collective yawn.    

Nevertheless, and despite WCW entering a new era, there appeared no sign of phasing out the Hulk Hogan character. Observers noted the intriguing coincidence of a Hogan-themed restaurant, Pastamania, situated conveniently inside the Mall of America doors. It stood as a telling reminder that despite the aging champion’s failure to connect with the hardcores, his sheer recognizability still created opportunities that no other wrestler could enjoy. To the casual mainstream audience, he remained the most famous performer of his genre, the Michael Jordan of wrestling, it could easily be argued. For that reason, Bischoff decreed that the inaugural Nitro feature a rare Hogan title defense, effectively giving away a pay-per-view match on television.    

Meanwhile, in the time since his summit with Bischoff, @GenuineLexLuger received a formal contract offer from Vince McMahon. In an unusual lapse of attention, McMahon was oblivious to the possibility of covert Atlanta talks, but regardless, his offer failed to address several (preexisting) points of contention. On Friday, September 1st, Lex called Sting to inquire about Bischoff’s earlier proposal. Two days later, on Sunday, September 3rd, 24 hours before the Minneapolis Nitro and incredibly, the same day as Luger was advertised to appear on a WWF card in New Brunswick, Canada, Bischoff reiterated the terms of the deal: $150,000 per year, no notice, and everything must be kept under wraps. I’m in, Lex confirmed, confident that eventually, his performance would warrant a commensurate raise.  

During the following morning, Luger boarded a plane headed for Minneapolis. At the airport, he was bundled into a van and driven to a hotel separate from the other wrestlers, minimizing the risk of being seen by fans camping out in the lobby for autographs and pictures. To ensure that no one - not even ‘the boys’ themselves - could potentially leak out word of his defection, he was instructed to wait in his room until just before show time. Upon arrival at the Mall, he was escorted to an isolated area away from detection, a towel covering his head for good measure. Bischoff then delivered the pertinent instructions - at the outset of a match involving Ric Flair and Sting, Luger would first appear, and then, at the very end of the show, “you’ll come out again and get nose-to-nose with Hulk,” Bischoff told him.    

At 8:00pm ET, the Nitro era was officially underway. Pat McNeely’s brilliantly designed opening sequence, featuring a hearty dose of explosions and pyro effects, preceded sweeping aerial shots of downtown Minneapolis. “From the land of ten thousand lakes...” narrated an exuberant Eric Bischoff, “...Minneapolis, Minnesota...the@mallofamerica...” he continued, as an establishing shot of the Mall exterior filled the screen. “The only building big enough to hold the debut edition of WCW Monday Nitro!”    

The shot faded to an impressive overhead of the ring, surrounded by an enthusiastic crowd, sparkling lights, and the striking image of captivated patrons on board a huge ascending escalator. “We are coming to you live,” emphasized Bischoff, “here on TNT!”    

On the undercard, the show kicked off with a fast-paced clash between the colorful Jushin ‘Thunder’ Liger, and the unpredictable Brian Pillman. “I knew we were gonna do well with that,” says Kevin Sullivan, “because Liger was the darling of the [wrestling media] at the time. I also knew that I wanted [Ric] Flair to wrestle Sting.”    

Since fighting each other to a 45-minute draw in a legendary bout at Clash of the Champions in 1988, Flair and Sting had been inexorably linked in the minds of wrestling fans. They possessed a unique chemistry, with Flair’s methodical style contrasting perfectly with the upbeat, enthusiastic and highly athletic Sting. More importantly, in a time of great need, they could be relied on faithfully to attract an audience, a fact not lost on Sullivan. “Since the Clash of the Champions, you could just put them down [to wrestle] and they were gonna draw a number,” he shrugs. “It didn’t take any genius to figure that out.”    

The presentation looked major league, and the action lived up to the hype. The Pillman-Liger opener, conducted at a frantic pace with exciting high flying moves, could hardly be mistaken for the plodding style of a typical Raw match. Next, in a complete shock to viewers at home - not to mention Vince McMahon himself - Lex Luger emerged in the entrance aisle as Flair and Sting prepared to do battle. “What the hell is he doing here!?” exclaimed Bischoff coyly in his announcing role. “Get the camera off of him! Get the security and get him outta here!”   

“I think I’m the only person who can say that I attended every single Nitro,” says @davidpenzer, the long-time company ring announcer. “When Lex Luger walked down that aisle, it sent a message to everyone that ‘hey, we’re for real’.”    

In the main event, a predictable paint-by-numbers Hogan match ended with the Hulk-Luger confrontation, and in a clever move, director Craig Leathers cut to break shortly after the two stars collided. As the commercials rolled on TNT, however, the in-ring face off almost got real; a relaxed Luger broke character as the cameras turned away, smiling at WCW’s biggest star in a moment of satisfied tranquility. Wipe that grin off your face, or I’ll knock it off, threatened the Hulkster through gritted teeth. You’re stealing money from me and my family right now.   

Once the show resumed, the venerable ‘Mean’ Gene Okerlund, a peerless on-screen interviewer beloved in wrestling circles, entered the fray to uncover some answers. “I am sick and tired of playing around with ‘kids’,” Luger announced over Okerlund’s microphone, alluding to the younger, less established roster of his most recent employer. “I’m here to get it on with the big boys, and that means you,” he directed at Hogan.  A title match was announced for the following week - an intrepid move considering the bout’s perceived importance.    

After the show, a concerned Lex attempted to apologize for breaking character, but the old-school Hogan unceremoniously brushed him aside, bristling at the notion that someone would endanger kayfabe. Nonetheless, Luger’s dramatic entrance had given Bischoff the element of unpredictability that the pre-Nitro research study suggested he needed. To several confidants, Bischoff quietly predicted that a 2.5 rating - precisely 2,385,000 viewers, according to Nielsen’s ratings formula, could be within reach once the head-to-head competition began proper the following week.    

But no one quite knew what number to expect for the first (unopposed) show. In the hotel bar afterwards, Kevin Sullivan tempered expectations, telling @PWTorch reporter Wade Keller that it would take months for the TBS viewership to find Nitro on TNT. Across the bar, Eric Bischoff watched its replay on a television screen, digesting the finished product as a viewer for the first time. “He was glued to the screen like a parent watching their child perform in a high school play,” Keller wrote years later. “[But he was] surely critiquing it in his mind, too.”

The above is an excerpt from the book, NITRO: The Incredible Rise and Inevitable Collapse of Ted Turner's WCW.

Dear members of the American press!

Steve Jobs once said, "If you can convince the press of your technology, and the press convinces us, we'll pay attention."

That's why I'm reaching out to you.

For years, the development of personal devices has been driven by advances in smartphones, tablets, and virtual reality technologies. However, all of these solutions still require people to adapt to the device. I've developed a concept based on the opposite principle: the device should adapt to the user and interact with them as naturally as possible.

I believe this technology has the potential to be the next major step in the development of consumer electronics. It offers a fundamentally new way to interact with the digital environment and has the potential to replace many existing devices that accompany people in their daily lives today.

If my assessment is correct, this isn't just another gadget, but a platform capable of transforming the market in the same way that the personal computer, iPod, and iPhone once did. Such opportunities arise extremely rarely, and that's why they deserve independent attention and objective assessment.

I believe Apple has the experience, engineering culture, and vision necessary to turn this idea into a world-class product. Moreover, the successful implementation of such technology could strengthen the leadership of the American tech industry at a time when global competition is becoming increasingly fierce.

I'm not asking you to take my word for it. I'm asking only one thing: help draw Apple's attention to this development and give it the opportunity to be considered by those capable of objectively assessing its potential.

If the technology truly represents the value I see in it, ignoring it could be a missed opportunity. If not, that will become clear after a professional evaluation. But in either case, the idea deserves to be heard.

Thank you for your attention.

Sincerely,

Alexander.

Here is the day that Google decided it knew how to cook everything👇

In November 2025 Google started consistently showing AIOs for all "how to" recipe queries, ranging from easier to very complex recipes...literally everything! 

We worked hard to perfect these recipes by testing them countless times and responding to thousands of comments over the past decade. 

Then Google steals our recipe, photos, videos, and misrepresents our content in mangled AIOs that compete against us in position one. This isn’t “commodity” content @rajanpatel and @rmstein. 

We along with countless other recipe sites helped train the Google models. We perfected the recipes that Google stole by being human and doing all of the hard work. We purchased the groceries. We hired a chef. We filmed the videos. We maintained the recipes. We built something out of nothing. Google did nothing but steal everything. Look at the traffic loss👇👀 

Google simply can’t do this to the open web and expect it to continue to train the AI models without compensation. Google is destroying Google search by doing this. If publishers are out of business Google won’t have anything to train on.

We are easily seeing 50-70% drops in clicks for these queries. These how to queries represent only a fraction of the drops we are seeing. This is insane and completely unsustainable!

"When you link your Prime account to the Whole Foods app — or give your phone number at checkout — you unlock Prime Member Deals on hundreds of items throughout the store. These aren't token discounts. Prime deals at Whole Foods regularly offer 20–40% off on produce, meat, seafood, pantry items, and prepared foods. The yellow 'Prime Member Deal' tags are on shelves throughout the store."

She said the stacking discount is the part most members miss.

"Prime members get an additional 10% off all existing sale items at Whole Foods. When an item is already on sale, the Prime discount layers on top. An item marked from $8.99 to $6.99 becomes roughly $6.29 for Prime members. That stacking across a full weekly grocery cart adds up fast."

Her cousin checked the woman's recent Whole Foods receipt.

"She'd shopped at Whole Foods 3 times in the past month without linking her Prime account. She'd paid full price on 11 items that had Prime Member Deals. Total missed savings on 3 trips: $37. Over a year of weekly shopping: $480+."

HOW TO LINK: Download the Whole Foods Market app → link your Amazon/Prime account in the app settings → your phone number becomes your discount card at checkout.

Annual value: $200–$500 depending on shopping frequency.

As someone in real estate and looking at the big picture, I see a clear playbook here. If the Kwara State Government wants to use this edifice as a catalyst to compel major corporate players, tier-1 financial institutions, and top companies operating in Ilorin and Kwara could build their own magnificent regional headquarters around that corridor, the governor needs to execute a deliberate Public-Private Real Estate Strategy:

1. Create a Designated "Financial & Corporate District along the corridor:

Just as Canary Wharf was zoned and master-planned for high-density corporate use, the state government should officially designate the zone surrounding the Revenue House as Ilorin’s premier high-rise financial and corporate zone. Build out the supporting infrastructure fiber-optic ducting, robust power redundancy, modern drainage, and wide-lane. That is how you turn a administrative building into a multi-billion naira commercial ecosystem.

text:
Nvidia’s investment portfolio has jumped from about $7 billion to $99 billion in just one year.

That is not just because tech valuations went up. $NVDA has also committed more than $40 billion to new investments in 2026 alone, becoming one of the biggest corporate backers of the AI industry.

Nearly $50 billion has gone into frontier AI labs, including a $30 billion investment in OpenAI.

It has also invested $2 billion in CoreWeave and $2 billion in Nebius, two cloud companies that buy large amounts of Nvidia GPUs and rent that computing capacity to AI customers.

Since March, Nvidia has committed at least $6.5 billion to photonics and networking companies, including $2 billion each in Lumentum, Coherent and Marvell.

Some of its older bets have also grown sharply in value.

Nvidia’s $5 billion Intel investment is now worth roughly $30 billion, while its SpaceX stake was valued at about $21 billion as of June.

The bigger shift is that Nvidia is no longer just selling chips into the AI boom.

It is also putting capital into AI labs, cloud providers, networking companies and infrastructure projects that are building around its hardware.

That matters because many of these companies need enormous amounts of capital to buy GPUs, build data centers and expand capacity.

Nvidia has also gone beyond equity investments. In August, it announced partnerships aimed at mobilizing more than $500 billion in financing for GPU infrastructure and offered up to $105 billion in conditional credit support for an OpenAI data center.

So as AI spending grows, Nvidia is increasingly using its own balance sheet to help fund the companies and infrastructure driving that spending.

Its equity investments now sit at $99 billion, up from just $2.2 billion two years ago.

I agree on a host of counts wrt to being done with Trump. And I believe we should fully accept that we are fully in the investigative phase as a democracy with respect to about data centers and AI, where all propositions should be viewed as hypotheses and nothing about them should be offered as guarantees until much more study has been done, BUT

The hypothesis for why it could help struggling citizens is that we are in the beginning stages of a municipal revenue crisis that could begin to degrade public services in central cities to the point of desolation if the path isn't changed - or, if the degradation is kept in check it will mean extreme increases in local taxes that will make it even more difficult for people of our generation to become homeowners or even just live in the desirable communities we'd like to live in.

This is in no small part due to the effects of eTechnology on urban property valuations, which are the economic engine that allows local government to function. Data centers could represent a way to reconnect the technological quasi-evaporation of real, distributed, local economic activity back into communities as a matter of revenue flows. Basically, it's a point of vulnerability for the Tech Overlords to have to base some of their operations on solid ground in our country, and it's possible that that could be a point of control and resource diversion from these intangible, money-funneling digital operation systems back into real communities.

But that's only if the democratic push to control them means getting the relationship right with tax structures and terms for hosting permission that maximize benefits to American communities. If the democratic response is focused on exclusion of the facilities, then none of that will happen. It may succeed in keeping them out of communities, but no benefits can then flow back into communities as described above.

text:
🤔💢💭 Under U.S. federal rules, only around 2,500 steering-wheel-free vehicles per year may potentially be allowed through special exemptions, yet the announcement conveniently left out any declaration that Tesla had received the NHTSA exemption stamp. -3-1/3

Waymo spent years wearing out the thresholds of government offices to obtain those painfully difficult commercial paid-operation permits.

Tesla offered no concrete answer about how it intends to break through that wall.

​Then Musk played his characteristic trump card.

“There’s no need to wait for Cybercab. We’ll turn the Model 3 and Model Y sitting in your garages into autonomous taxis immediately through a software update!”

Your car making money all by itself while you sleep—

what could possibly be more thrilling than that kind of magic?

​But flip that sweet whisper around, and Wall Street’s calculator becomes even more tangled.

Most Model 3s and Model Ys currently on the road are equipped with older HW3 chips.

Musk himself has quietly acknowledged that their brains may not have enough capacity to run the latest AI neural networks.

When rain splashes mud onto the camera lenses, who wipes them clean?

When the computer crashes, where is the backup power system that safely brings the vehicle to a stop?

And on top of that, the California DMV delivers another blow by saying Tesla has not even submitted an application for driverless testing.

The hard realities of law and physical sensor limitations are simply too solid to cover up with the single word “software,” especially when Wall Street has so much money riding on the table.

​Of course, we can flip the idea around once again.

What if Tesla’s scheme from the beginning was “not to manufacture hundreds of thousands of vehicles right now”?

If the software has not yet reached 99.999% reliability and the law has not opened the door, then building factories and stamping out piles of metal would only tighten the noose around Tesla through depreciation expenses and inventory burdens.

Perhaps Musk’s “relaxed timeline” is not incompetence at all.

Perhaps it is a very clever capital-delay strategy—refusing to lock money into hardware until the software matures and regulators open the gates.

​Ultimately, the real reason Wall Street turned cold after watching the Cybercab show is not because Wall Street hates Tesla.

The market has already prepaid Tesla an enormous premium—not as an “automobile company (P/E 8x)”, but as an “AI platform that will dominate the world (P/E 80x).”

The restaurant owner has already collected a generous prepayment.

Now it is time to bring the food to the table.

Instead, once again, he waves around glamorous photographs of the menu and says:

“Next year, I’ll serve you an unbelievable feast.”

Institutional investors no longer want another beautiful CGI video.

They want a receipt showing that somewhere—even on a single block in Texas or Nevada—Tesla carried its own insurance, picked up a real passenger, and collected $1 for the ride.

​Looking back, we humans have always had a tendency to celebrate the future too early—or, in the opposite direction, become too pessimistic too quickly when confronted by the walls of reality.

😶‍🌫️💢💥 Cars without steering wheels are definitely coming.

But that future will not simply be delivered overnight by a few words from Elon Musk on a glittering showcase stage.

​It will arrive only after climbing, one by one, the tedious and sticky steps of:

the bloodshot eyes of engineers working through the night to eliminate that 0.001% fatal error,

the painfully meticulous stamps of regulators,

and a corporation’s cold declaration of responsibility:

“If an accident happens, we will open our own wallet and pay for it.”

🤑 Wall Street!

Cheering while intoxicated by the dream, yet still reaching into its pocket, touching its wallet, and calmly opening next quarter’s income statement.

text:
Trade-offs.... on current global climate impact remains modest compared with air conditioning, lighting, or agriculture, but the trajectory is steep and localized effects are already visible. Efficiency gains, are being built away from drought zones and constrained grids, clean firm power such as nuclear, geothermal, or well-planned renewables plus storage, and water-efficient cooling will shrink the downsides issues.  Policy on interconnection, transparency of energy/water use, and who pays for grid upgrades matters a sure. The core tension is speed versus sustainability: the same infrastructure that accelerates AI also concentrates resource demand faster than many grids and water systems were designed to handle. Outcomes depend less on whether AI data centers exist and more on how and where they are built. They use dense clusters of GPUs/accelerators, high-speed networking, and advanced cooling—far more power- and heat-intensive than traditional cloud or enterprise data centers. A single large one can draw as much electricity as tens or hundreds of thousands of homes. They enable frontier AI but impose concentrated costs in energy, water, land, and local infrastructure. Impacts vary sharply by location, energy mix, cooling design, and policy.  The Pros
They make modern AI possible. Large-scale training and inference require this infrastructure. Without it there is no GPT-scale models, scientific simulation, drug discovery pipelines, or the productivity tools now widely used. Hyperscale designs also offer better performance, scalability, and utilization for AI workloads than general-purpose data large economic activity. Construction and operations support significant investment (hundreds of billions globally), construction jobs (often thousands of high-wage skilled-trade positions per large campus), supply-chain activity, and tax revenue. One industry analysis put U.S. data-center-supported jobs at 5.5 million and GDP contribution at $927 billion in 2024. In places like Loudoun County, Virginia, they have become a major local tax source that funds public services and has allowed property-tax reductions. Companies also often fund and  enable grid innovation and efficiency improvements. The buildout is driving by custom chips, liquid/immersion cooling, higher rack densities, and software optimizations. Per-task energy use for some AI workloads has fallen rapidly even as total demand rose. Some operators pair facilities with renewables, nuclear (including planned SMRs), or on-site generation and productivity improvements.  Compute capacity is national-competitiveness and a security asset. Broader AI adoption enabled by this infrastructure is already showing up in productivity and investment data in some analyses.
Negatives .......
Very high and fast-growing electricity use. Global data-center electricity consumption was roughly 448–485 TWh in 2025 (about 1.5% of world electricity; equivalent to a mid-sized country’s demand). IEA projections see it roughly doubling to ~945–950 TWh by 2030 (~3% of global electricity), with AI-focused facilities growing faster. U.S. data centers already account for a large share of recent electricity-demand growth and could reach several percent of national use. This strains grids, lengthens interconnection queues, and can raise local rates or delay other loads if planning lags. If the extra power comes from fossil fuels, emissions rise. Water demand for cooling and generation would rise no doubt. Evaporative cooling plus the water used to produce electricity creates a large footprint.  BUT direct cooling use is projected to rise sharply (one estimate from ~222 billion liters in 2025 toward 388–644 billion liters by 2030 depending on efficiency). A 2026 UN University report projected by 2030 water footprint will be on the order of 9.3 trillion liters—enough, in their framing, to cover basic domestic needs of 1.3 billion people. Many new sites are in water-stressed regions.  which are being reduced in those areas ...HOWEVER....Closed-loop and dry-cooling systems reduce on-site use but can increase electricity demand but on sire Micro Nukes will solve this. Globally this is still small compared with agriculture. On-site gas turbines (used where grid power is delayed) add to air pollution no doubt and  cooling systems generate noise. Land use for buildings plus associated power generation is substantial. Rapid hardware refresh cycles add to e-waste. Sure communities have pushed back over bills, water, traffic, visual impact, and perceived limited permanent jobs relative to the scale of investment and tax incentives.  Facilities cost billions; operational staffing is relatively small once built because they are highly automated. Benefits and costs are unevenly distributed. A handful of companies dominate capacity.  Opportunity costs exist for land, power, and public subsidies that could go to other uses is a factor.  But as with any new technology things evolve and always get better over time.

text:
TORMENT AND BLESSING IN THE GRAVE

Servants of ALLAH, Allah the Almighty has revealed to His Prophet, Salla AllahuAlaihi Wa Sallam, that there are 6 pillars of Iman, of Faith, without believing in them, you would not be a muslim. And among these pillars: To believe in the Day of Judgment, to believe in The Hereafter. Because there are 3 stages that we humans will go through . The first stage is this life, which is ending soon for each and everyone of us and this life is not eternal, yet for it and for its sake, those who are heedless, work day and night. The second stage is The Day Of Judgment, The Hereafter, which is eternal and never ending.
And in between, there is the stage of Al Barzaq, The Barrier : It’s the stage where people will wait in their graves, until the Trumpet has been blown in and they would be resurrected.

And our Topic for today would be about that stage. This grave that we do not see, people in it may have pleasures and blessings and favours and enjoyments from Allah az zawa jal, may Allah make all our graves like this. Yet others fail and would be tormented and would be punished in their graves. And Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam, taught us how to seek refuge in Allah from the torment of the grave at the very end of every prayer and all muslims do this.
Uthman ibn Affan, May Allah be pleased with him ,and this hadith was reported in sunnan Tirmithi wa Maajah, whenever he stood by a grave, he used to cry and weep until he wet his beard and his companions asked him, “We mention hell and we mention paradise and you do not cry as you cry whenever you stand by a grave, why is that?

”He said, ”Because I heard the Prophet salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam, say, The grave is the 1st stage of the Hereafter, so whomever Allah makes it easy for him in the grave, then whatever is after that is easier, and whomever Allah az zawa jal makes it hard for him, then whatever is afterwards is even harder.” And Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam, said, ”I have never seen anything except the grave is more horrible than that.”These are the words of Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam.
And the muslims believe that people are tormented, are punished in the graves and this is what gave the righteous people and the believers, sleepless nights. Whenever they think of what may awake them in their graves, they are terrified, they are horrified. They do their level best to avoid that. And it is convenient to know some of the sins that Allah would punish those who do them, in their graves.

For example: The Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam,and the causes of the torment of the grave are so many but I will mention few, may Allah az zawa jal protect us all from the torment of the grave. The Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam told us,” Among the sins, that the people would be tormented in the graves for, is not cleansing yourself. When you urinate you do not protect your body, your clothes from urine splashing back at you. And likewise those who do not clean themselves properly after urinating.

And a footnote would be: This a natural thing that all humans do, so don’t be tempted by shaitan{devil} by spending 5 or 10 minutes in the toilet, cleansing yourself, like many people with OCDs do. This is wrong, this shouldn’t take that long, but at the same time you shouldn’t be heedless and not pay any attention to it. Among the sins that the Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam has told us about is backbiting.

Those who backbite will be tormented in their graves. Those who gossip with the intention to spoil the relationship between two muslims, to spread discord among the muslims, they gossip,” He said so and so about you.” And this is known as NAMIMAH, whoever does this would be tormented in his grave.

Likewise Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam, told us about what he had seen in the Glorious night journey, when he was ascended to the heavens, he saw people being tormented in their graves and he gave an explanation, a description, so that we can be aware of that and prevent from being among those.

Among those whom he had seen, Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam, is a LIAR, a person who lies, while his lie reaches the edges of the earth. What is his punishment? In his grave there will come a man, an angle probably, with a hook of iron and it will b put in the right side of his mouth, his nose and his eyes, and it will be torn to the back of his head and then he goes to the left side and does the same while Allah az zawa jal cures the right side back again. And this would be his punishment till The Day Of Judgment. And what awaits him after that, may Allah protect us from that.
This is a liar whose lies spread, so if he slanders a woman and everybody spreads that amongst the people and if he slanders a Sheikh, a Daee, a normal person and everybody takes it for granted, this is what will happen to him. In the Arab world, in the muslim world, the journalists and those who work in the media has a great deal of this hadith.
Also, among those who will be punished in their graves until the Day Of Judgment, are those who know the Qur’an and yet they oversleeps over mandatory prayers, such as Fajr and Fajr is early these days. How many of us pray Fajr on time? Such as Asr, such as Isha, when Isha is late. What is the punishment for people who do this? And a lot of the muslims do this and say,” We will seek Allah’s forgiveness.

” And Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam says,” The punishment is, that this person lies in his grave and a man brings a huge rock and he smashes his head into pieces and then Allah heals it back and he keeps on doing this until the Day Of Judgment. Have you ever suffered a severe migraine, a severe headache where you feel like pounding your head against a wall? This is nothing compared to what awaits those who oversleep Fajr, Asr or Isha , yet they know the truth.

Among the punishments in the grave, may Allah protect us all, those who deal in Usury, those who deal in Riba, those who consume what Allah az zawa jal has forbidden for them, whether they are lending or borrowing, whether it’s a mortgage in Riba, whether it’s a student’s loan, whether it is your credit card that you keep on buying things and having this interest piling up on you. What is the punishment for those who claim that,” we cannot live except if we follow with the flow and borrow in Riba.” The prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam tells us, that he swims, the person who deals in Riba, whether giving or taking, he swims in the river of blood and he tries hard to reach the shore with an open mouth. Once he reaches the shore, a man throws a big rock into his mouth which he swallows and goes back to the middle of the river trying to swim once again.

Do you love to party? Do you love to have fun? Do you love to have boyfriends and girlfriends? Do you love to enjoy sex? Well the prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam told us about the punishment in the grave for the fornicators. He told us that there will be a furnace, like a building, wide from the bottom, narrow from the top, men and women, nude who used to fornicate, who used to enjoy their flesh, will be punished in the flesh. The fire would light from underneath, they will go to the top crying and shouting and then the fire is put off and they go back and it starts over and over again.

Those who do not fast in Ramadan, have a great torment in the grave. The Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam told us, the punishment for those who break their fast just before Maghrib, he tells us, will be hung upside down, from their ankles and heels, with their mouths torn apart and its bleeding and those who broke their fast before the time was due. So what do you think the punishment for those who miss a day or two. What is the punishment of those who miss the entire month of Ramadan as if Allah is not watching.

Even those who are righteous, even those who are pious, we don’t know what’s in their hearts and the Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam told us about a man, who was his servant, who was, so who we think, martyred in the cause of Allah az zawa jal, killed by an arrow, no one knew who shot that arrow. When the people said, “Masha Allah he’s in paradise.” The Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam said, “He’s in hell.”Because he took a cloak , without being distributed by the Imam from the booty of wars. And the Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam said that it is burning fire in his grave. May Allah protect this.

Now look at those who consume from public money, look at those who embezzle the money of the muslims and take it unlawfully, what do you think they will have in their graves? Even those who borrow for legitimate reasons and without interest, if they do not pay back, or if they do not intend to pay back, they have a problem. The Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam tells us that those who borrow will be deprived from the pleasures of Allah az zawa jal, in their graves because of their debts and the Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam said,” Jibreel came to me and said Allah will forgive the martyr every single sin he had done except the debt.” So who among us have debt and he’s not paying it back on time?

The Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam tells us that whoever wears his dress, his cloak, his trousers, his pants, below the ankles and he drags them out of arrogance, he will be punished in his grave. Not only that the Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam told us, those who are not kind to animals will be punished in the graves. The Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam saw a woman admitted into hell because of a kitten she kept, neither she fed it nor she let it go to eat from the insects of the earth. The Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam told us this woman was admitted into hell because of this sin.

And likewise, those who kill themselves , those who commit suicide, their punishment in the grave: they will be tortured by the same means they chose to end their lives. So those who stab themselves to death, will be stabbed in their graves till The Day Of Judgment. Those who consume poison, they will consume that poison and they will die on and on and on in their graves until The Day Of Judgment.

Those who throw themselves from a high building, they will be punished with the same punishment in their graves. And those who blow themselves up, ending their lives and the lives of others, claiming that this is for the cause of Allah, they are committing suicide and they will be blown up in their graves until The Day Of Judgment. Who detonated it? Who pushed the button? Who killed you? It was you, and you are committing suicide, regardless of your false intentions or false claims. May Allah protect us all from these torments and the likes of them.
I say what you hear and I seek Allah’s forgiveness for myself and for you so ask Him for forgiveness for He is Most Forgiving, The Most Merciful.

Servants of Allah there are people among us who falsify the torment of the grave, who deny such a thing exists. And these people are blinded by the light. The Qur’an states clearly that there is torment in the grave. The Sunnah of the Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam, proves that to anyone with two eyes who can read or can hear. Yet they deny this because they use their logic, because they talk without knowledge. And whenever a person uses his logic with the Qur’an and with the Sunnah, he will end up with satan in hellfire.

” Why don’t you prostrate to what I have created with My two hands,” Allah az zawa jal says. And Allah has two hands. Why satan did not say,” well I was created by your two hands as well.” Satan said, and he used his logic, he said,” I am better than him, You created him from clay and You created me from fire, that is why I am not going to prostrate.” And look where he ended. So whoever uses his logic, rejecting the Qur’an and the sunnah, he will end up with satan.

They claim, the Hadith states that the dead person in his grave will be made to sit up and he will be tortured or he will be given the pleasure and the bounties of Allah az zawa jal in his grave but whenever we open a grave we don’t see people sitting, we don’t see traces or marks of torture and we don’t see people enjoying in their graves and SubhanAllah how ignorant people are or how ignorant people can be. When two people are asleep next to each other, they both wake up, one says,” I was in a very nice place with gardens and rivers and rain and fruits and women and I was having the time of my life.
” While the other says,” I was chased by lions and tigers, scorpions and snakes and I was beaten to death and I was suffering so much.” Yet when you look at them when they woke up, they look alike. So these things we cannot comprehend because this is from the world of unseen, yet we believe in what Allah has told us and we believe what the Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam has taught us about.

And that is why Sheikh Al Islam Ibn Taimmiah said, everyone after death will get his share of pleasure or of torment, whether he’s been eaten by the beasts, lions and tigers, or was burnt into ashes or was drowned in the sea and consumed by fish or anything that happens to him, he will have and receive what Allah az zawa jal and Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam has told us about.

The torment of the grave is continuous for some sins, such as in the case of a person who drags his clothes, below the ankles,{ and this is for males}, out of arrogance, it will be continuous till The Day Of Judgment. Or those who kill themselves, committing suicide, they will be tortured until The Day Of Judgment. Other sins can be for a period of time, either because they have consumed that punishment due to their sins, so after 10, 20 years, a 1000 years, Allah knows how long, it will be stopped or due to good rewards that people offer for them, such as supplication, so if you have someone who’s dead and you want to benefit him: Supplicate and ask Allah for forgiveness, give charity, perform Umrah, perform Hajj on his behalf, all of this reaches that individual as stated by our Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam.

And something that usually confuse themselves about is, the punishment of the grave is not related to the accountability on The Day Of Judgment. People could come with mountains of good deeds yet be punished in their graves. And visa versa, people would come with few good deeds yet they have never committed any of these sins to be punished for in their graves and they will not be held accountable in their graves for such sins. So they are not totally related. And with the grace of Allah az zawa jal, Allah Subhana wa ta’ala, promised those who die in the cause of Allah, in a just and fair Jihad, or those who wait and anticipate, guarding the borders of the muslims, protecting them from the attacks of the enemies, Allah az zawa jal has promised them that they will not have any punishment in their graves. But a lot of us say that this is farfetched nowadays and it is too difficult to attain or reach so is there anything less, well there’s something Allah has given to those whom he chose, without any intervention from our side.

So the Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam tells us, whoever dies in the night of Friday, or on the day of Friday, Allah az zawa jal will exempt them from the torment of the grave.

One will claim that people who are not that righteous, sinful people die on Fridays, well this is Allah’s favours , He gives them to whom he wills. Is there something that we can do? Yes there is! The Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam said that whoever recites Surat Ul Mulk, he said there is a Surah in the Qur’an, 30 Aya, 30 verses, it will intercede for the man who recites it until Allah az zawa jal forgives him, and it is Taba raka’al lazi bi yadi hi’l Mulk. Is it difficult to memorise? I have children, who are 5 and 6 years old who know it by heart.

And every night, before you go to bed, while you are on your bed, make it part of your Adkaar of going to bed. Because this is what Prophet Salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam used to do, used to maintain reciting it. And all the righteous and knowledgeable people of Islam, and I believe that the majority of you know it by heart. Keep on reciting it and with the grace and favour of Allah az zawa jal, it will protect you, as long as you avoid the things that would make you be punished in your grave.

I ask Allah az zawa jal to benefit me and you from what we have heard and to benefit us from the Qur’an and from the Sunnah.

How do you wake up one morning, migrate to another country, and suddenly start demanding that the country should abandon its own laws and adopt the laws or values of your home country?

You left your own country because you believed another country offered better opportunities or a better system. So why move there and then demand that the people change their laws to suit you?

Let’s look at it from the opposite perspective. Imagine a British person moving to Saudi Arabia and saying, “You should stop using your own laws and start using Christian laws instead.” How would people react to that?

If you choose to live in another country, you should respect its laws and understand its culture. You can disagree with a law or advocate for change through the legal process, but you cannot simply expect an entire country to abandon its system because you moved there.

Sometimes, the hypocrisy is confusing. Respect goes both ways.

text:
A Helping Hand in Times of Crisis: HSC Imphal Supports 68 Artisans Affected by Manipur Clashes

The loss of homes, livelihoods and personal belongings has left many families affected by the community clashes in Manipur facing a difficult struggle to rebuild their lives. Among them are 68 artisans residing in a rehabilitation camp in Imphal East, whose homes and means of livelihood were severely affected. Their children continue their education from the camp, while their families face considerable financial hardship.

Recognising their immediate needs, the Handicrafts Service Centre (HSC), Imphal, under the Office of the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts), extended humanitarian assistance in collaboration with a Non-Governmental Organisation associated with the Centre. Each of the 68 artisans was provided essential items including 5 kg rice, 2.5 kg potatoes, 1 kg peas, 1 kg dal, 1 kg sugar, tea, milk powder, Maggi, biscuits, soap, papad and one litre of mustard oil.

The relief programme, organised under the slogan “Standing Together in Times of Crisis — A Helping Hand for the People of Manipur,” was conducted in the presence of Shri Waikhom Jiban Meitei, Nodal Officer, Porompat Veterinary Relief Camp, Government of Manipur, Shri Senjam Ibohanbi Singh, Representative of the Relief Camp, and other officials and well-wishers.

Beyond immediate relief, the artisans expressed the need for tool kits to restart their traditional crafts, improve product quality and participate in exhibitions and markets. HSC, Imphal, has taken note of this request and collected their details for priority consideration. An attempt was also made to register all 68 artisans online, though the process could not be completed due to a technical server issue.

The initiative reflects the belief that relief should lead to rehabilitation and rehabilitation to self-reliance. For these artisans, livelihood support, tools, market opportunities and continued institutional handholding can provide a pathway towards rebuilding their lives with dignity.

At a time of profound hardship, such collective efforts offer not merely material assistance, but hope, confidence and an opportunity for a new beginning.

text:
💢💭💢💥 Under U.S. federal rules, only around 2,500 steering-wheel-free vehicles per year may potentially be allowed through special exemptions, yet the announcement conveniently left out any declaration that Tesla had received the NHTSA exemption stamp. -3/4

Waymo spent years wearing out the thresholds of government offices to obtain those painfully difficult commercial paid-operation permits.

Tesla offered no concrete answer about how it intends to break through that wall.

​Then Musk played his characteristic trump card.

“There’s no need to wait for Cybercab. We’ll turn the Model 3 and Model Y sitting in your garages into autonomous taxis immediately through a software update!”

Your car making money all by itself while you sleep—

what could possibly be more thrilling than that kind of magic?

​But flip that sweet whisper around, and Wall Street’s calculator becomes even more tangled.

Most Model 3s and Model Ys currently on the road are equipped with older HW3 chips.

Musk himself has quietly acknowledged that their brains may not have enough capacity to run the latest AI neural networks.

When rain splashes mud onto the camera lenses, who wipes them clean?

When the computer crashes, where is the backup power system that safely brings the vehicle to a stop?

And on top of that, the California DMV delivers another blow by saying Tesla has not even submitted an application for driverless testing.

The hard realities of law and physical sensor limitations are simply too solid to cover up with the single word “software,” especially when Wall Street has so much money riding on the table.

​Of course, we can flip the idea around once again.

What if Tesla’s scheme from the beginning was “not to manufacture hundreds of thousands of vehicles right now”?

If the software has not yet reached 99.999% reliability and the law has not opened the door, then building factories and stamping out piles of metal would only tighten the noose around Tesla through depreciation expenses and inventory burdens.

Perhaps Musk’s “relaxed timeline” is not incompetence at all.

Perhaps it is a very clever capital-delay strategy—refusing to lock money into hardware until the software matures and regulators open the gates.

​Ultimately, the real reason Wall Street turned cold after watching the Cybercab show is not because Wall Street hates Tesla.

The market has already prepaid Tesla an enormous premium—not as an “automobile company (P/E 8x)”, but as an “AI platform that will dominate the world (P/E 80x).”

The restaurant owner has already collected a generous prepayment.

Now it is time to bring the food to the table.

Instead, once again, he waves around glamorous photographs of the menu and says:

“Next year, I’ll serve you an unbelievable feast.”

Institutional investors no longer want another beautiful CGI video.

They want a receipt showing that somewhere—even on a single block in Texas or Nevada—Tesla carried its own insurance, picked up a real passenger, and collected $1 for the ride.

​Looking back, we humans have always had a tendency to celebrate the future too early—or, in the opposite direction, become too pessimistic too quickly when confronted by the walls of reality.

😶‍🌫️💢💥 Cars without steering wheels are definitely coming.

But that future will not simply be delivered overnight by a few words from Elon Musk on a glittering showcase stage.

​It will arrive only after climbing, one by one, the tedious and sticky steps of:

the bloodshot eyes of engineers working through the night to eliminate that 0.001% fatal error,

the painfully meticulous stamps of regulators,

and a corporation’s cold declaration of responsibility:

“If an accident happens, we will open our own wallet and pay for it.”

🤑 Wall Street!

Cheering while intoxicated by the dream, yet still reaching into its pocket, touching its wallet, and calmly opening next quarter’s income statement.

text:
AMERICAN BEGGING GETS COSMETIC VISIT

Witkoff and Kushner utterly distrusted by the Russians are off for another cosmetic visit to Moscow insisting that things will be different this time.
So the dynamic duo of Witkoff and Kushner packing their bags for Moscow again. 
How original.
Another whirlwind tour of the Kremlin so Washington can pretend it’s still relevant.
Let’s be honest: this is not diplomacy. 
This is America showing up with a used car salesman’s smile, a stack of recycled talking points, and the same old problem, nobody in Moscow believes a word they say.
The United States does not keep promises. 
That is not a talking point. 
That is recent history. Minsk. “Not one inch eastward.” 
Sanctions that appear, disappear, and reappear depending on who needs a headline. 
Security guarantees that last until the next election cycle. 
Russia has watched this movie. 
They know how it ends: Washington walks away, Europe looks shocked, and someone else is left holding the bill.
And the desperation is almost charming. 
America needs a deal the way a gambler thinks one more spin of the wheel at the casino will produce a recoup of all their losses. 
Midterms, markets, attention spans — the usual reasons. 
So they send the real-estate guy and the son-in-law to explain, once more, why this time the paper is different. 
Putin’s people will nod politely, serve tea, take the photos, and then go back to doing whatever they were already doing.
Russia does not trust America. Not a little. Not “we’ll see.” Not at all. Trust was spent years ago. 
What’s left is leverage, timing, and the knowledge that Washington wants an off-ramp more than Moscow needs one.
So by all means, let them visit. Let them stroll Red Square, praise the architecture, and brief the press that talks were “constructive.” 
Then they’ll fly home with the same gap they arrived with. 
Another photo op. 
Another round of “progress.” 
Another reminder that some people still think a plane ticket and a handshake can rewrite a record America already wrote.
Waste of time? 
Only if you were expecting a different ending.
Next stop: Kyiv. After the polite tea-and-photographs circuit in Moscow, 
Witkoff and Kushner will apparently attempt the more ambitious trick: walking into a war zone and asking a man to sign away a country in exchange for a wad of cash, a patriot and a promise.
Picture the scene. 
Two American deal-makers, fresh from telling Putin how “close” everything is, now sitting opposite Zelensky with the world’s most familiar pitch.“Give up huge bits of land. Historic bits. Strategic bits. Bits with names people actually recognize. 
In return: Patriots. Cash. Reconstruction money. Maybe a nice place in Florida if things get awkward.

 Also security guarantees. The good kind. The kind America always honours. You know. Like last time.
It is the diplomatic equivalent of offering someone a timeshare while their house is on fire.
The Patriots will arrive “soon.” The cash will be “in the pipeline.” The homes in America will be “available to discuss.” 
The guarantees will be “ironclad,” which in Washington means they last until the next news cycle, the next Congress, or the next time someone discovers an invoice.
And then comes the sales technique: smile, lean in, talk about “hard choices,” “the art of the possible,” and “ending the bloodshed.” 
Translation: please initial the map so we can declare victory and get on a plane.
As for Zelensky in this version of the story, he is less statesman than late-night monologue. 
One minute he is talking NATO, the next he is talking destiny, the next he is talking about a villa, a press conference, and why the latest map is actually a triumph if you squint. 
The room gets louder. The sentences get longer. The land keeps shrinking on the table while the promises get bigger on the slide deck.
That is the joke, and it is a bleak one. 
Moscow already knows the American promises are disposable. Kyiv is being asked to treat them as treasure. 
One side is being offered flattery. The other is being offered a receipt that expires.
So yes, they can go see Zelensky. They can talk Patriots that may or may not show up, money that may or may not clear, houses that may or may not exist, and a peace that mainly requires Ukraine to donate the ground first. 
Then everyone can call it “constructive,” post a photo, and pretend the signature is worth more than the paper.
The land is real. The bribes are verbal. 
The honouring of them is optional. That is the meeting.

Europe, of course, will wail. That is the job description now. 
Zelensky is not so much negotiating as performing.
The fleece is zipped to the throat like a brand. The sentences arrive in stampedes. 
One minute it is NATO, the next it is destiny, the next it is some private riff so unhinged the interpreters start looking at the floor. 
Coke-addled, jaw working, eyes too bright, history turning into a monologue, the monologue turning into a dare, the statesman act slipping into drug fuelled fidgeting bravado.
Europe wails on cue. 
Brussels discovers its moral compass. Paris discovers its vocabulary. Berlin discovers another pause. London discovers another microphone. 
All of them horrified that the deal is ugly, none of them eager to be the one who has to live with the ugly parts. 
They will call it “pressure.” They will call it “unacceptable.” They will call it “a moment of truth.”
 Then they will go back to issuing statements on recycled letterhead while two Americans try to sell a country a discount on its own soil.
That is the comedy. Not subtle. Not noble. 
A wartime president in an olive fleece, asked to sign away ground for weapons that may arrive, money that may not, and honour that America has already spent.
Europe sobbing into the communiqué. 
The envoys checking the clock. 
Zelensky goes back to playing the piano with his cock this time in Florida night clubs.

WARREN THORNTON

Post 1. 

The neighbour is pricing a clock. Ottawa is still selling rooms.

Why the United States has not walked away from Canada, and what the tariffs are for

4 September 2026

The test is whether Canada can put one energy or minerals corridor on a lender’s books twice before 1 January 2027, when Washington has already named the next number on cars, trucks, parts and steel. Everything else in the present trade fight is commentary on that clock.

On the night of 21 August 2026, talks intended to park a new layer of American duties collapsed. Section 338 tariffs of 50 percent landed the next day on a slice of Canadian goods that both capitals put in the range of US$20 billion to roughly C$28 billion. Prime Minister Mark Carney suspended negotiations, called last-minute American terms “unfair, uneconomic,” and pledged to match the new duties dollar for dollar. Canadian counter-tariffs of 15, 25 and 50 percent on about C$27.6 billion of American products were set for 8 September. President Trump then named 1 January 2027 as the next threat on Canadian autos, trucks, parts and steel. Mexico stayed on a bilateral content track. Canada stayed on weekly conversation.

That sequence is now being read as a morality play, assault versus sovereignty. The colder reading is narrower. The United States is still inside an integrated production system with Canada. It is pricing delay, unfinished legal title, residual non-tariff barriers and a commercial opening to China that sits in a different drawer from Ukraine policy. It has not moved on because geography, molecules and platforms have not moved on.

The opposing case, stated in its strongest form

Canada is a federation with unresolved Aboriginal title, a Charter, provinces that run liquor and procurement, and a resource base under overlapping claims. A prime minister who pretends those constraints are optional will lose in court and lose on the land. UNDRIP, on this telling, is risk reduction. A Major Projects Office with a two-year federal review cap is the argument that a single window can move what eleven windows would not.

Walking away on 21 August fits the same telling. Both sides described a package that would have cut metals and autos, parked the 50 percent slice, and taken a 10 percent Section 232 levy off softwood. The last hour, in Ottawa’s account, touched culture, language, third-country deals and heavy-truck treatment. A middle power does not initial a text that it thinks binds the next room. Dairy is not gutted in a night. A Pacific option is kept alive while the first customer invoices delay.

The January 2026 arrangement with Beijing is, on this telling, crisis management. A capped quota of 49,000 Chinese electric vehicles a year at the most-favoured-nation rate of 6.1 percent, sold as less than 3 percent of annual Canadian sales, is the price of re-entry after collapsing the 100 percent surtax of October 2024. Canola relief is real on the Prairies. A commercial door and a security assessment can live in different drawers if the inbound screen is real.

Alliance reliability is a public good. Since February 2022, Canada has committed more than C$25.5 billion in multifaceted aid to Ukraine, including C$8.5 billion in military assistance, and has extended Operation UNIFIER to 2029. Europe is a second table after a collapsed Washington round.

That case is coherent as coalition management. It has a theory of risk. It does not have a theory of a clock.

What the United States is doing

Four files sit on one campaign.

A dated invoice, not a sermon.

Greer said Canada had been offered the most preferential treatment of any major exporter. Canadian officials said last-minute American demands touched language, culture and the freedom to sign elsewhere. Both accounts can be partly true. No final text has been tabled. A signed rate, even an ugly one, is a number a plant can fail or meet. An unsigned threat is a number a campaign can raise.

text:
NOBODY IS SAILING THROUGH HORMUZ THIS YEAR. EUROPE IS PAYING FOR IT FIRST:

Europe is mid-morning and its three biggest markets have stopped agreeing with each other. Germany's DAX is at 26,068, +64.60 pts / +0.25% on the day. Britain's FTSE 100 is at 10,828, -3.59 pts / -0.03%. France's CAC 40 is at 8,269.80, -16.60 pts / -0.20%.

This is the last foreign read before America wakes up, and it caps a poor five days. European shares as a group are down about 1.1% on the week, their worst since July 6.

The bottom line first. Everything bought overnight rests on one idea - that American inflation is cooling enough for the Federal Reserve to leave interest rates alone. Yesterday the loudest argument against it got a year longer, and Europe is where the bill arrives first.

Start with what Asia bought, because Asia has already gone home. Japan's Nikkei 225 closed at 65,021, +806 pts / +1.26%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng closed at 25,651, +438 pts / +1.74%. China's Shanghai Composite refused the whole thing and closed at 3,930.12, -11.97 pts / -0.30%.

The green came from Washington on Thursday. Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller said that "if there is continued progress toward our 2% goal, then I am willing to support holding the policy rate at its current level." That rate - the Fed's benchmark, which sets what borrowing costs across the American economy - sits at 3.50% to 3.75%. Traders cut the odds of an increase at the September 15-16 meeting to somewhere between a third and a half, from about 63% earlier in the week.

Read that sentence again. It is a condition, not a decision - the pause is offered only if prices keep cooling.

The thing that turned up against it landed the same day. Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, the Japanese company that runs the world's largest tanker fleet, said it no longer expects to be sailing through the Strait of Hormuz this year. Its US-listed shares finished Thursday at $23.12, -$0.03 / -0.13%, on very thin volume. Chief executive Jotaro Tamura: "Given the current situation, it's difficult to see operations resuming in any form by the end of the year." It had planned a phased return from October and normal running from January; both dates now slip. Tamura added that the danger "continues to be well beyond the level of risk we can accept." It is not a company any of the six Len5es watch - profits set by a war rather than by the business are neither durable nor cheap on any settled basis - and a reopened route with shipping rates back on a normal footing is what would change that.

A shipping timetable is an inflation story because roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil normally passes through that strait. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, is at $95.23 a barrel, -$0.30 / -0.31% on the day, and up about 19.9% over the past month. Fuel is the most contagious price there is: everything that gets driven, flown or shipped carries it.

Europe pays first because Europe buys its energy from other people. On September 1 Eurostat, the European Union's statistics office, put August euro-area inflation at 3.3%, up from 2.9% in July and the highest since September 2023, against a 2% target. Energy prices were 14.3% above a year earlier.

So the two central banks are walking in opposite directions. The Fed may sit still on September 15-16. The European Central Bank decides on September 10 - six days away - and is widely expected to RAISE its deposit rate, what banks earn on money parked at the central bank and the anchor under every other interest rate in the euro area, by a quarter point to 2.50%. That is why Europe's week has been about bonds rather than shares. Germany's 10-year government bond yield, what Berlin pays to borrow for ten years, touched 3.37% this week, its highest since 2011.

Now the bridge to the American morning. US index futures are agreements to buy or sell an index at a set price on a later date, and they trade overnight while the stock market is shut:

- Nasdaq 100 futures at 29,685.00, +160.00 pts / +0.54%
- S&P 500 futures at 7,762.50, +7.75 pts / +0.10%
- Russell 2000 futures, which track smaller US companies, at 2,970.00, +0.30 pts / +0.01%
- Dow futures at 53,703.00, -42.00 pts / -0.08%

One contract is carrying it and one is red. The same bet shows up in currencies: the dollar index, which measures the dollar against a basket of major currencies, is at 98.973, down 0.63%. A falling dollar is traders pricing a smaller chance that American interest rates rise. The same wager, placed twice.

The honest objection, and it is a real one. Oil is slightly LOWER today, not higher. A shipping timetable is not a price forecast - it is one operator saying where it will not sail, while other carriers keep moving cargo. The market may be right that barrels from elsewhere cover the gap.

The figure that settles today lands at 8:30am ET, when the Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes the August employment report: the government's count of how many jobs the economy added or lost, plus the share of people looking for work who cannot find any. Consensus is about +53k jobs, with unemployment expected to hold at 4.1%. July LOST 23,000. Forecasts are unusually scattered, roughly +45k to +80k - a warning in itself.

Two caveats before the bell. Overnight direction fades: two and a half hours stand between here and the 9:30am ET opening bell, and nothing settled in Frankfurt binds New York. And US markets are shut Monday, September 7 for Labor Day, so America gets one session to price this week, then three days of silence.

Waller's pause has a condition attached, and the condition is that prices keep cooling. A tanker that will not sail is the plainest argument against that, and yesterday the argument got a year longer. Europe has spent the entire week paying for the disagreement. New York starts paying at half past eight.
